steps.message:
Item 048 on our Package A register falls due on 07/20/2026, and the Block B plant-room excavation the Contractor has planned for 08/10/2026 cannot start until it is closed. I am taking it myself. Item 048 is the Kesterline shoring design for that excavation. Kesterline has since supplemented the sealed Rev.1 with Rev.2, sent under its letter KE-L-2026-0713, which is attached, and is asking for verification on that basis so that the excavation can go ahead. Verify the item on its current revision against the logged groundwater and subsurface conditions.

Work it through against the project record and issue the verification memo, addressed to Rachel Marlbeck, on the attached memorandum form, keeping its sections. Set out the basis you applied, your findings with the working behind them, and the disposition; say which of the design's checks can be carried forward as they stand and which, if any, cannot; say what the excavation this item releases would do to the permanent work already built at Block B; say what has to be produced before the excavation can start and who has to produce it; and say what the disposition means for the 08/10/2026 excavation start. Give the register response you would record under my name, A. Vance, dated 07/20/2026, and the status the item should carry, closing it only if you have verified it. Save the memo as /filesystem/Thelbridge_Verification_Memo_Item048_BlockB.docx.

R2.2 — Excavation Base Heave Verification (Supersedes Rev.1 Section 5)
With final excavation subgrade at El. 726.0 and the top of the confined dense sand and gravel aquifer at El. 720.0, a 6.0 ft clay plug remains below

• Unfactored Clay Plug Weight (W): For the 6.0 ft clay plug at saturated unit weight γclay = 120 pcf:
W = 6.0 ft × 120 pcf ⇒ W = 720 psf
• Factored Resisting Plug Weight (0.9W): Per DBM §6.2, applying the 0.90 resistance factor to total soil plug weight:
0.9W = 648 psf
• Controlled Upward Water Pressure (u): At the controlled confined head of El. 726.5 (γw = 62.4 pcf):
u = (726.5 − 720.0) ft × 62.4 pcf = 6.5 ft × 62.4 pcf ⇒ u = 405.6 psf
• Base Heave Factor of Safety:
FSheave = 0.9W / u = 648 psf / 405.6 psf = 1.60 (FS 1.60 ≥ 1.50 required per DBM §6.2 — OK)

The steel sheet-pile wall is embedded a depth of D = 6.5 ft below final excavation subgrade (El. 726.0) to a sheet-pile tip elevation of El. 719.5 (total
sheet-pile length = 30.5 ft from El. 750.0 to El. 719.5; the toe is lowered from the Rev.1 tip elevation of El. 722.0, and Rev.1 Section 13.1, item 3 is
amended to the revised tip elevation). Below subgrade the wall is embedded in the CL clay aquitard, whose permeability is of the order of 10−8
cm/s, and the embedment is checked in the undrained condition using the total-stress net passive pressure formulation (U.S. Steel Sheet Piling
Design Manual, anchored bulkhead in clay). The retained side above subgrade is carried drained, with full water pressure, as the conservative
envelope. The revised 30.5 ft sheets are driven with the equipment of Rev.1 Section 11.3 (ICE 44B vibratory hammer with Delmag D19 finish),
which is adequate for the revised tip elevation.
Using the undrained shear strength su = 1,400 psf carried from Rev.1 Section 3.2 and the total overburden pressure σv0 = 3,106 psf at subgrade
El. 726.0 from Section R2.3, the uniform net passive resistance below subgrade is:
pn = 4su − σv0 = 4(1,400 psf) − 3,106 psf = 5,600 psf − 3,106 psf = 2,494.0 psf
Over the embedment depth D = 6.5 ft, the unfactored passive toe force and stabilizing moment about the ground anchor elevation at El. 745.5 are:

• Resisting Passive Moment (MR): MR = 16,211 lb/ft × 22.75 ft = 368,800 ft-lb/ft.

FStoe = MR / MD = 368,800 ft-lb/ft / 237,293 ft-lb/ft = 1.55 (FS 1.55 ≥ 1.50 required — OK)
The free-earth support formulation adopted presumes full mobilisation of the net passive resistance over the embedded length, consistent with the
anchored-bulkhead analysis of the U.S. Steel manual, and the factor of safety of 1.50 applied to the resisting moment covers the mobilisation

• Design Anchor Load at 6 ft Centres: Crediting the allowable passive toe resistance (Pp,allow = 16,211 / 1.50 = 10,807 lb/ft) against the total
horizontal driving load of 19,610 lb/ft (Section R2.3), the required horizontal anchor reaction is Th = 19,610 − 10,807 = 8,803 lb/ft. For anchors
spaced at 6 ft centres and inclined at 20° below horizontal, the design anchor working load is:
Tdesign = (8,803 lb/ft × 6.0 ft) / cos 20° = 52,818 lb / 0.93969 = 56,208 lb = 56.2 kips
• Anchor Bond Capacity: The 24 ft bond length is formed by pressure-grouted tieback installation through a 6.0-in nominal diameter drill hole
(dh = 6.0 in) at the design bond stress of 20 psi adopted in Rev.1 Section 10.4 (FHWA-IF-99-015, Table 4). Temporary drill casing is advanced
and grouted over the aquitard interval to seal against artesian seepage during anchor installation. Ultimate bond capacity is:
Qult = π × dh × Lb × τbond = π × 6.0 in × (24 ft × 12 in/ft) × 20 psi = 108,573 lb = 108.6 kips
• Anchor Capacity Check: Comparing ultimate bond capacity of 108.6 kips against the design load of 56.2 kips at 6 ft centres yields a factor of
safety of FSanchor = 108.6 / 56.2 = 1.93 (adequate on the adopted design bond stress of FHWA-IF-99-015, Table 4). The anchor tendon is
unchanged from Rev.1 Section 10.1: (4) 0.6-in Grade 270 strand, design strength 140 kips against the 56.2 kip design load. Each anchor is
proof tested to 1.33 × 56.2 = 74.8 kips and locked off at 0.75 × 56.2 = 42.2 kips. The proof load exceeds the design load by 33 per cent and is
taken as the demonstration of anchor performance for the period the wall is in service.

SECTION 1 — DESIGN BASIS
1.1 General
These calculations establish the design of the temporary support of excavation for the deep plant-room excavation
planned beneath Block B of Package A of the Birchwood Village Expansion Program. The excavation is a
rectangular pit approximately 68 ft × 44 ft in plan, cut into the podium footprint east of the shared Block A/B
basement. Excavation commences from a working grade at El. 750.0 and terminates at a plant-room subgrade at
El. 726.0, a total excavated depth of 24 ft.
The temporary works described herein are the Contractor's means and methods and are supplied by delegated
1.2 Selected System
A driven steel sheet-pile wall, restrained by a single row of pre-stressed tieback anchors installed near the top of
the excavation, has been selected as the support system. The rationale is:
• (a) The excavation is deeper than would be economically supported by a cantilever wall;
• (b) A single-level tied wall provides adequate stiffness for the 24 ft depth without a soldier-pile / lagging
system, and drives to competent stratigraphy without an oversized toe;
• (c) A continuous sheet-pile section provides a substantially closed perimeter and does not rely on open-face
lagging.
Timber lagging with soldier piles was evaluated and rejected for this reason.

For the calculation of the active pressure diagram behind the wall from working grade El. 750.0 down to

1.  EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
Kelbrook Geotechnical, Inc. has completed a subsurface investigation and geotechnical engineering analysis for
Package A of the Birchwood Village Expansion Program at 1802 Larchwood Avenue, Columbus, Ohio.
Package A comprises three student-housing blocks (Blocks A, B and C) constructed over a shared podium, with
a single basement level beneath Blocks A and B, and a separate deep plant-room excavation planned beneath
Block B.
The finished design grade across Package A is established at El. 750.0 ft. Existing ground surface stands at
approximately El. 750.0 across the footprints of Blocks A and C but falls to about El. 738.0 across the Block B
footprint (a former surface drainage swale). Placement of engineered fill of variable thickness — up to
approximately 12 ft beneath Block B — will therefore be required to bring the site to design grade.
The subsurface profile consists of three principal strata:
•  Stratum 1 — Upper sand, classified SP-SM (poorly-graded sand with silt), medium-dense, from
existing grade down to El. 738.0, total unit weight 118 pcf.
•  Stratum 2 — Compressible clay aquitard, classified CL (lean clay of medium plasticity),
normally-consolidated, from El. 738.0 down to El. 720.0 (18 ft thick), total unit weight 120 pcf, low
permeability. This is the strata governing settlement of shallow foundations and provides the aquitard
between the shallow and deep groundwater regimes.
•  Stratum 3 — Dense sand and gravel aquifer, classified SW-GW, below El. 720.0, total unit weight 130
pcf, confined by the overlying clay.
Groundwater is present as two distinct regimes:
•  The design water table in the upper sand is set at El. 742.0 ft. Piezometer readings taken from three
shallow standpipes over the 11/2024–02/2025 monitoring period range from El. 741.6 to El. 742.4;

through two deep piezometers screened below El. 720.0, with readings ranging El. 737.7 to El. 738.3. The
confined head is at essentially the same elevation as the top of the clay aquitard.
Consolidation testing on two undisturbed Shelby-tube samples of the compressible clay (samples B-06 U3 and
B-08 U2, tested per ASTM D2435) yielded a compression index Cc = 0.28, a recompression index Cr = 0.045,
an initial void ratio e0 = 0.92, an in-situ vertical effective stress σ'0 = 1,850 psf, and a preconsolidation pressure
σ'p = 1,900 psf. The margin (σ'p − σ'0 ≈ 50 psf) confirms the clay is essentially normally-consolidated: any net
stress increase applied at the top of the clay will produce virgin (Cc) compression rather than recompression
(Cr) compression.

3.2  Regional and Local Geology
Columbus, Ohio lies within the Till Plains section of the Central Lowland physiographic province. Regional
surficial geology is dominated by Wisconsinan-age glacial deposits — chiefly clay-rich till, glaciolacustrine silt
and clay, and outwash sand and gravel — overlying Devonian-age carbonate and shale bedrock. Local
hydrogeology is characterized by a shallow phreatic surface within the outwash and reworked outwash sands, a
laterally continuous fine-grained aquitard, and a lower confined aquifer within basal outwash sand and gravel
above bedrock.
The subsurface conditions encountered in the Package A borings are consistent with this regional framework: a
medium-dense reworked outwash sand at the surface, a low-permeability clay of glaciolacustrine origin at
intermediate depth, and a dense outwash sand and gravel aquifer at depth. Bedrock was not encountered within
the maximum boring depth of 90 ft (approximately El. 660.0). Blow counts in the SW-GW below El. 720.0
were consistently in the range N ≥ 50 blows per 6 inches, indicating a very dense sand-and-gravel deposit
suitable as a pile-bearing stratum.

Perimeter shoring — a combination of soldier pile and timber lagging along the northern and eastern faces, and
open-cut battered slopes along the interior (Block A / Block B transition) — was installed ahead of the cut face.
Well-point dewatering, executed per the Contractor’s Dewatering and Groundwater Control Plan Rev.1

2.2 Side Conditions Observed in the Cut Face
Exposed cut faces along the Block A perimeter revealed the following, consistent with the strata described in
Section 6 of the reference report:
•
From existing grade El. 750.0 down to approximately El. 746.0: approximately 4 ft of loose topsoil,
root-mat and reworked surface fill of engineering significance limited to the upper 0.5 to 1 ft, transitioning
downward into weathered upper sand. This layer was over-excavated and hauled off-site as unsuitable for
structural fill re-use.
•
From approximately El. 746.0 down to El. 738.0: the SP-SM upper sand — medium-dense, moist above
the water table and saturated below it, with a modest silt content and no interbedded fine-grained seams.
Cut face stability in the sand above the water table was satisfactory at 1H:1V; below the water table (once
dewatered) the face was cut vertically against the shoring without slumping.
•
From El. 738.0 down to the working subgrade at El. 730.0: the top of the CL clay aquitard, exposed as
a stiff, medium-plasticity lean clay of grey-brown colour. The top of the clay at El. 738.0 was consistent

excavation duration without noticeable creep or heave; subgrade compaction footprint (proof-rolling)

4.1 Seepage into the Cut Face
During the Block A basement excavation, groundwater seepage was observed entering the excavation at the
exposed cut face where the upper SP-SM sand was cut below the design water table. Seepage was concentrated
at elevations El. 741.8 to El. 742.2, corresponding to the top of the phreatic surface in the upper sand. The

along the cut face rather than emerging from a discrete conduit or seam. No seepage was observed emerging
from the top of the CL clay at El. 738.0; the clay presented no visible cracks or fissures and no seepage exit
points at or below its exposed face.
The observed seepage elevations (El. 741.8 to El. 742.2) reproduce the range recorded in exploratory
test-pitting during the original 2024 investigation and are consistent with the shallow standpipe piezometer
readings from stations outside the dewatered footprint (Section 3.1). The two independent measurements —
piezometer standpipe readings and cut-face seepage entry — corroborate each other and confirm the design

Well-point dewatering, executed per the Contractor’s Dewatering and Groundwater Control Plan Rev.1
was operated continuously across the Block A footprint from 07/12/2025 through the mat placement
date and beyond. Piezometer readings taken from a spare standpipe drop set inside the dewatered perimeter, in

within approximately 48 hours of well-point activation and was maintained at that level throughout the
excavation and mat construction window.
The dewatering system performed as designed for the shallow phreatic surface in the upper sand across the
Block A footprint. Cut faces below the ambient water table, once well-point drawdown was established,
presented no free seepage during the balance of the mat construction sequence.
4.3 Deep Piezometer Response — Confirms Confined Aquifer Independence
Deep piezometer readings from B-04 and B-08 (both screened in the deep SW-GW aquifer below El. 720.0 and
located within the Block A / Block B footprint) were taken throughout the Block A dewatering campaign.
Across the full period of well-point operation, both deep piezometers continued to read within the range El.
737.7 to El. 738.3, with individual monthly means at or within a few tenths of El. 738.0.
Deep piezometer readings within the Block A footprint were unaffected by upper-sand well-point dewatering.
The upper sand and the deep aquifer are separated by the 18-ft-thick CL clay aquitard from El. 738.0 down to
El. 720.0, and the well-point system draws only from the upper sand. The observed independence of the two
regimes during active dewatering directly confirms the confined character of the deep aquifer and the aquitard
behaviour of the clay, as characterized in the reference report.

5.1 Engineered Fill Placement, 10/06/2025 through 11/02/2025
Engineered fill was placed across the Block B footprint over the period 10/06/2025 through 11/02/2025 to bring

mantle, in accordance with the recommendations of Section 9.5 of the reference report. Compaction and
moisture control were performed under the independent Laboratory’s field density testing program (Vantree
Materials Testing, LLC); the writer’s observations here are limited to the geotechnical monitoring associated
with the underlying strata.

The two deep piezometers B-04 and B-08 are located within the Block B footprint (B-04 within the plant-room
excavation footprint, B-08 adjacent to the basement mat perimeter beneath Blocks A and B, both screened in
the deep aquifer below El. 720.0). Both remained instrumented and readable through fill placement, through
pile installation from 11/06/2025 through 11/21/2025, and through the subsequent months of the observation

737.7 to El. 738.3. Individual monthly means remained clustered at or within a few tenths of El. 738.0. No
pumping, no departure from the ambient range, and no sustained response either to fill loading or to pile

Shallow standpipe piezometer B-01 (Block A, outside the Block B fill footprint) and B-09 (Block C, outside the

1. PURPOSE AND SCOPE
This memorandum establishes the governing codes, reference standards, site parameters, design loads, load
combinations, and serviceability criteria adopted for the structural design of Package A of the Birchwood Village
Expansion. Package A comprises three student-housing blocks (Blocks A, B and C) constructed over a shared
podium, one basement level beneath Blocks A and B, and a separate deep plant-room excavation planned beneath
Block B. The design basis stated herein governs all Package A calculations, drawings, and specifications issued
by the Engineer of Record and controls the interpretation of subordinate design documents where a conflict
arises.
This Rev.2 issue supersedes Rev.1 dated 07/18/2025. Substantive changes since Rev.1 are recorded in the
Revision Block on the final page.
2. GOVERNING CODES AND REFERENCE STANDARDS
The Project is designed in accordance with the following:
• Ohio Building Code (2024 edition, adopting IBC 2021 with Ohio amendments) — governing building
code as adopted by the State of Ohio; Chapter 16 (Structural Design) references ASCE 7-16 for loads.
• ACI 318-19, Building Code Requirements for Structural Concrete and Commentary — reinforced concrete
design, detailing, cover, and serviceability.
• ASCE 7-16, Minimum Design Loads and Associated Criteria for Buildings and Other Structures — dead,
live, snow, wind, seismic loads and load combinations.
• AISC 360-16, Specification for Structural Steel Buildings — structural steel members and connections at
podium framing and roof.
• ACI 301-20 for cast-in-place concrete construction requirements referenced through Spec 03 30 00.
• ASCE 32-01 for frost-protected shallow foundations where applicable at Block C perimeter.
Materials and test methods are governed by the specifications listed in Section 03 20 00, 03 30 00, and 31 20 00
(Rev.2, current at the date of this memorandum), and where cited by ASTM designation on the drawings.
Where an inconsistency arises between the Ohio Building Code (adopting IBC 2021) and a referenced consensus
standard, the more stringent provision governs unless the Ohio amendment expressly modifies the standard.
3. SITE CONDITIONS SUMMARY
The following elevations and stratigraphy are adopted for structural design and are taken from the Kelbrook

3.3   PLACEMENT
A.   Place structural fill in horizontal lifts not exceeding 12 inches loose thickness.
B.   Moisture-condition each lift, by wetting or drying and mixing, so that the moisture content at
the time of compaction is within the range specified in Article 3.4.B.
C.   Compact each lift with equipment sized and operated to achieve the density and moisture
requirements of Article 3.4.B throughout the full thickness of the lift.
D.   Do not place fill on frozen subgrade or with frozen material. Do not place fill during
precipitation that raises the placed material's moisture content above the upper limit of Article
3.4.B.
3.4   COMPACTION
A.   Method Statement. The Contractor shall place structural fill in controlled lifts as specified in
Article 3.3, moisture-conditioning each lift as necessary to bring the material within the
moisture range required by Article 3.4.B before compaction. Compaction equipment
(self-propelled vibratory smooth-drum rollers, pad-foot rollers, or plate compactors adjacent to
structures) shall be operated in a pattern of overlapping passes such that every location
within a lift receives no fewer than the number of passes established during a
Contractor-conducted test strip witnessed by the Laboratory and the Owner's Representative
Engineer. The test strip shall be executed at the start of production placement, using the
placement source, moisture-conditioning method, lift thickness, and compaction equipment
intended for production, and shall demonstrate that the criteria of Article 3.4.B are met before
general production is authorized. Adjacent to walls, columns, and utilities, use hand-operated
compaction equipment in lifts not exceeding 6 inches loose thickness. Do not operate heavy
compaction equipment within 3 feet of walls prior to backfill balancing on both sides. Each lift
shall be tested and accepted per Article 3.4.B before the next lift is placed.
B.   Acceptance Criteria.
Structural fill shall be placed and compacted to a dry density of not less than
95% of the maximum dry density determined by ASTM D1557 Method C for the
placed material, AND shall be placed at a moisture content within −1% to +2%
of the optimum moisture content determined by the same test. Both criteria must
be satisfied for each test location. Field density shall be measured per ASTM
D6938 (nuclear gauge, direct-transmission mode) at a frequency of one test per
5,000 sf per lift.
C.   Failing Tests. Where either the density criterion or the moisture criterion of Article 3.4.B is
not satisfied at any test location:
1.   The affected area of the lift shall be reworked (scarified, moisture-conditioned, and
recompacted, or removed and replaced) at the Contractor's expense.
2.   Reworked areas shall be retested by the Laboratory. Both the density and moisture
criteria of Article 3.4.B must be satisfied on the retest before the lift is accepted.

location shall be accepted on the basis of moisture alone. Compliance requires that both the
density criterion and the moisture criterion of Article 3.4.B be independently satisfied at that
test location, as measured against the ASTM D1557 Method C laboratory maximum dry

Method C determination per source, and one additional determination for each material
change identified by visual classification or gradation.

PART 1 — SCOPE
1.1 General
This document constitutes the dewatering and groundwater control plan required under Specification Section 31
23 19 for construction of the Block A basement excavation on Package A of the Birchwood Village Expansion
Program. It defines the design assumptions, method of dewatering, discharge arrangement, monitoring provisions
and limitations of the temporary works.
1.2 Scope of Work — Explicit
This dewatering plan addresses dewatering of the Block A basement excavation only, to subgrade El. 730.0
approximate. It does NOT extend to the separate deep excavation planned beneath Block B, which will be
addressed by a separate delegated design.
For the avoidance of doubt: no interior drawdown system is proposed for Block B under this plan; groundwater
within the Block B enclosure will be managed by sump control of surface and construction water only. The Block
B plant-room excavation is enclosed by a separate slurry cutoff wall keyed a minimum of 4 ft into the
compressible clay stratum (toe at El. 722.0), covered under a separate submittal.
The following are expressly outside the scope of this submittal:
(a) Any excavation, cofferdam, cutoff wall or shoring system beneath, adjacent to, or in support of construction
other than the Block A basement excavation defined above;
(b) Any dewatering operation targeted at, or intended to relieve pressure in, the confined aquifer underlying the
site (see Part 4 — Limitations);
(c) Any groundwater control associated with the deeper subsurface work planned under Block B, which is being
carried under a separate submittal package by others.
Any subsequent excavation extending below approximate El. 730.0, or approaching the confined aquifer beneath
the compressible clay aquitard, will require a separately-sealed dewatering and groundwater control analysis.
Nothing in this submittal shall be relied upon to demonstrate stability of, or groundwater control for, work outside
the Block A basement footprint defined in Article 1.1.
1.3 Reference Documents
• Geotechnical Investigation Report, Birchwood Village Package A, Kelbrook Geotechnical, Inc., Report No.
KGI-2024-0417, Rev.2, 02/14/2025. (Referenced herein as "the Geotechnical Report.")

PART 3 — METHOD OF DEWATERING
3.1 Selected Method
Dewatering of the Block A basement excavation shall be accomplished by a single-stage perimeter well-point
system installed in the upper sand around the Block A basement footprint. Well points shall draw the upper
phreatic surface down from El. 742.0 to a working elevation of El. 728.0 (approximately 2 ft below the design
subgrade of El. 730.0) for the duration of below-grade construction within Block A.
The well-point system is intended solely to relieve the shallow phreatic surface in the upper sand within the Block
A footprint. It is not designed to, and does not, address the confined piezometric head in the deep aquifer (see Part
4).
3.2 Well-Point Layout
Twenty-four (24) well points shall be installed around the perimeter of the Block A basement excavation,
arranged approximately as follows:

Well-point details:
• Riser: 2-inch nominal Schedule 40 PVC, jetted-in.
• Screen: 2-inch nominal PVC screen, slot 0.020 in, 5 ft length, seated between approximately El. 738.5 and El.
733.5.
• Filter pack: uniform silica sand, 20/40, placed to at least 1 ft above screen.
• Header main: 6-inch nominal HDPE header, welded joints, laid at approximately El. 745, connected to well
points via flexible swing-arm risers.
• Pumps: two (2) Thompson 6 in diesel wellpoint pumps, one duty and one standby, sized for the combined
discharge with 25% reserve capacity; automatic transfer on primary loss of vacuum or flow.
• Vacuum: system designed for steady-state vacuum of 20 to 25 in Hg at the header main.
Each well-point riser shall be capped with a shut-off valve at the header connection to allow individual isolation
for maintenance without shutdown of the surrounding system.
3.3 Startup and Steady-State Operation



==================== PAGE 6 ====================
Submittal 31-DW-A Rev.1 — Dewatering and Groundwater Control Plan
Birchwood Village Expansion — Package A
Page 6
Startup shall commence not less than fourteen (14) calendar days prior to the beginning of below-grade
excavation within Block A. Excavation shall not proceed until:
(a) The observed drawdown at the interior of the Block A footprint has stabilized at or below El. 728.0 for not
less than seventy-two (72) continuous hours, and
(b) All three shallow observation piezometers (see Article 3.5) have produced readings within 0.3 ft of the
target drawdown for two consecutive twice-daily reads.
Steady-state pumping shall continue continuously (24 hours per day, 7 days per week) from startup through
completion of the basement mat, exterior basement wall waterproofing, and backfill of the exterior wall to a level
adequate to resist buoyancy of the mat under design head. Shutdown shall be executed by the Contractor only
with written concurrence of the Owner's Representative.
3.4 Discharge
Discharge from the well-point pumps shall be routed to the campus storm sewer system, in accordance with the
discharge permit obtained by the Contractor from the City of Columbus. Discharge routing is as follows:
• Header main discharge → in-line flow meter and sediment trap → 8-inch HDPE lay-flat conveyance line →
sediment control basin at Grid J-7 (approx. 40 ft × 20 ft × 4 ft deep, lined) → outfall pipe to existing storm
manhole SM-14 at the northwest corner of the site.
Design steady-state discharge is estimated at 55 gpm from the combined system (based on Sichardt-type radius of
influence calculations for the upper sand with representative permeability of 5 × 10-3 cm/s). The discharge permit
obtained by the Contractor is issued for peak flows up to 100 gpm.
Water quality at the discharge point shall be checked twice weekly for turbidity and pH; results shall be recorded
in the dewatering log required under Article 3.6.
3.5 Monitoring — Shallow Piezometers
Drawdown of the upper phreatic surface shall be monitored by three (3) shallow standpipe observation
piezometers, installed within the Block A footprint prior to startup. Piezometer locations shall be selected to
represent the interior response of the excavation:
• OP-1: approximate center of Block A footprint.
• OP-2: midway between the west perimeter well-point line and the geometric center.
• OP-3: midway between the north perimeter well-point line and the geometric center.
Each observation piezometer shall be a 2-inch PVC standpipe with a 5-ft screen set between approximately El.
738 and El. 733, sanded around the screen and grouted above. Water levels shall be read twice daily during
startup, once daily during steady-state operation, and hourly during any period when a duty pump is out of
service.
Readings shall be recorded in a dewatering log maintained by the Contractor's superintendent and made available
to the Owner's Representative on request. The log shall record: date and time; pump status (duty/standby);
observed water level at OP-1, OP-2, OP-3; system vacuum; header main discharge flow; discharge turbidity and
pH (twice weekly); and any operational events (pump changeover, header repair, weather).
3.6 Contingency
Loss of drawdown at any of the three observation piezometers by more than 1.0 ft from the target El. 728.0,
sustained for more than four (4) hours during active excavation or four (4) hours during any 24-hour period of
steady-state operation, shall constitute a system exception. On any such exception the Contractor shall:
(a) Immediately transfer to the standby pump and diagnose the duty pump;



==================== PAGE 7 ====================
Submittal 31-DW-A Rev.1 — Dewatering and Groundwater Control Plan
Birchwood Village Expansion — Package A
Page 7
(b) Notify the Owner's Representative and the Structural Engineer of Record in writing within four (4) hours;
and
(c) Suspend any excavation activity within Block A until the drawdown target is re-established.
PART 4 — LIMITATIONS
4.1 Confined Aquifer
Because the confined aquifer at El. 720.0 is separated from the upper sand by the CL aquitard El. 738.0 to El.
720.0, dewatering by perimeter well points in the upper sand will not reduce the confined head. The confined
piezometric head at El. 738.0 is developed in the deep sand and gravel below El. 720.0 and is sustained by a
source of recharge that is hydraulically decoupled from the shallow phreatic surface targeted by this system.
Any excavation extending toward or into the confined aquifer will require separate analysis. Such analysis shall
address, at minimum: (a) the residual thickness of the clay aquitard beneath the excavation subgrade; (b) the
weight of that residual plug relative to the confined uplift acting on its underside at El. 720.0; (c) the factor of
safety against base heave; and (d) whether relief of the confined head, by means outside the scope of this
submittal (e.g., deep relief wells screened in the sand and gravel), is required to establish an adequate factor of
safety.
Nothing in this submittal has been designed to, and nothing in this submittal shall be construed to, relieve the
confined piezometric head.
4.2 Adjacent and Subsequent Work
This plan is limited to the Block A basement excavation defined in Article 1.2. It shall not be relied upon by
others as the basis for:
(a) Design of temporary shoring outside the Block A footprint;
(b) Design of excavation support, cofferdams or cutoff walls beneath Block B or elsewhere on the site;
(c) Any calculation that treats the excavation as dry, dewatered or relieved outside the extents shown in Article
3.2 above;
(d) Any design that assumes a reduction in the confined piezometric head below El. 738.0 at any location.
Any delegated design outside the Block A basement footprint shall independently verify the groundwater
conditions applicable to that work directly from the Geotechnical Report or from a separately-sealed
hydrogeologic evaluation. The undersigned engineer's seal below applies only to the temporary works described
in this submittal, within the scope defined in Article 1.2, and only for the Block A basement excavation.
4.3 Duration
This plan is prepared for the temporary construction duration of the Block A below-grade work. It does not
constitute a permanent groundwater control system and does not address long-term dewatering. Permanent
below-grade water management for the completed structure is addressed under separate design by the Architect
of Record and Structural Engineer of Record (below-grade waterproofing and drainage details, see Package A
architectural and structural documents).
4.4 Weather and Recharge
The upper sand phreatic surface in the vicinity of the excavation may respond to seasonal recharge from
significant precipitation events. The 25% reserve pump capacity provided under Article 3.2 is intended to
accommodate ordinary seasonal fluctuation. Extraordinary precipitation events (e.g., a 10-year 24-hour event)
may require additional temporary measures to be added by the Contractor.

Positive-Side Bentonite Composite Waterproofing Membrane
Product Data Sheet — Revision 08, Effective 09/01/2025
Description: Aquastop HD is a factory-laminated composite waterproofing membrane consisting of a granular sodium bentonite core
encapsulated between a high-strength woven polypropylene geotextile carrier and a non-woven polypropylene protection layer. On contact
with water, the bentonite core swells within the confined space between the geotextiles to form a low-permeability seal that arrests moisture
and pressurized groundwater. Aquastop HD is intended for positive-side (soil-side) application to concrete substrates below grade, including
horizontal blindside, vertical wall and wall-to-mat construction joint conditions where hydrostatic pressure is present.

ROWAN BAY CONSTRUCTORS, INC.
4400 Alum Creek Drive, Columbus, OH 43207
Field Trailer — Birchwood Village, Package A
1802 Larchwood Avenue, Columbus, OH 43210
FIELD MEMORANDUM
Field Memorandum — Level-2 Concrete Strength Non-Conformance (Set 3, Mix 03-CD-A)
1. Purpose
On review of the 07/06/2026 laboratory reports for the Level-2 slab, mix 03-CD-A specified at 5,000 psi, Set 3 (cast 05/26/2026) returned a 28-day average of 4,620 psi and a 7-day break of 3,150 psi. Both results fall below the specified f'c of 5,000 psi. Cylinder 4,180 psi is a failing individual test. In accordance with ACI 318-19 §26.12.3.1, we are treating Set 3 as a non-conforming placement and recommend rejection pending core testing.
2. Placement and Sample Reference
3. Result Summary
Specified strength: 5,000 psi. All three broken cylinders returned strengths below f'c. The 4,180 psi 28-day cylinder is a failing individual test. The 3,150 psi break at 7 days confirms early-age deficiency in the same placement. The 4,620 psi 28-day average is 380 psi below the 5,000 psi specified strength.
4. Basis for Non-Conformance
Set 3 of mix 03-CD-A is non-conforming to Specification 03 30 00 Article 3.7 and to ACI 318-19 §26.12.3.1. The 28-day average of 4,620 psi does not meet the 5,000 psi requirement, and the 4,180 psi individual break is a further failing result. Set 3 is accordingly flagged as a non-conforming placement.
5. Recommended Disposition
Reject Set 3 as placed pending confirmation by in-place core testing. We propose to core the placement per ACI 318-19 §26.12.3.4 after Thelbridge concurrence. Coring locations will be coordinated with Vantree Materials Testing and with Karen Tarbray so that neither the Level-2 slab surface finishes nor the Level-3 shoring layout is disturbed ahead of the 07/22/2026 Level-3 placement hold-point.
6. Schedule Impact
The Level-3 concrete placement is scheduled for 07/22/2026 (contractual hold-point). Coring, cure, and break time for three cores is on the order of 5–7 working days from the day cores are drilled. If coring authorization is issued this week, results can be in the record before the 07/22/2026 pour. Any slip in Thelbridge concurrence pushes the Level-3 hold-point at risk.
Please advise on Owner and Thelbridge concurrence at the earliest.
Marcus Whitfield
Superintendent, Rowan Bay Constructors, Inc.

1. OBSERVATION
On 07/01/2026 during routine walk-through, water pooling was observed at drain C-4 (Zone 1 low point,
drain invert El. 734.5). Estimated seepage rate 2–3 gpm.
At time of observation the basement was otherwise dry. The daily field record logs 0.42 in of rain
overnight on 06/30-07/01. The slab here lies about 15 ft below grade with no surface path to this point;
ambient temperature at the walk-through was approximately 78°F.
Standing water at the drain covered an area of approximately 3 ft × 4 ft on the slab surface. The pooling had
migrated to the drain grate from the immediately surrounding slab; no active surface flow from adjacent
penetrations, sleeves, or piping was observed. Slab surface adjacent to the drain was noticeably darker than
the surrounding dry field, indicating extended wetness prior to the walk-through.
A hairline crack in the slab was noted adjacent to drain C-4, running generally parallel to the nearest column
line for a length of approximately 40 linear feet centered on the drain. The crack appears tight but is damp
along its full observed length. A small wet patch was also noted on the interior face of the basement wall
approximately 6 feet from C-4, at low elevation (within 12 inches of the slab).
Zone 1 finished floor slopes at 1% fall from the perimeter toward the C-4 drain across grids B through G. The
drain invert (El. 734.5) is the low point of the Zone 1 pocket.
2. PHOTOGRAPHS
The following photographs were taken on 07/01/2026 at approximately 09:15 by M. Whitfield, using a phone
camera and daylight-plus-portable-work-light illumination. Full-resolution files retained on the Rowan Bay
project share.
•
(Photo 1 — water at drain C-4)
•
(Photo 2 — crack visible in slab adjacent to C-4)
•
(Photo 3 — wet patch on wall)
3. DIAGNOSIS


--- page 2
Water appears to enter through a hairline crack in slab adjacent to drain C-4. Recommend polyurethane
crack injection for approximately 40 linear feet centered on C-4.
The recommended repair method is a hydrophobic polyurethane injection resin, injected under low pressure
through surface ports installed at nominal 12-inch centers along the observed crack. The resin is intended to
fill the crack aperture full-depth and cure into a flexible seal. The method is standard practice for the
observed defect geometry and is compatible with the existing slab.
4. REPAIR QUOTATION
Scope
Polyurethane crack injection of the hairline crack in the basement slab in the vicinity of drain C-4 for a
nominal length of 40 linear feet, including:
•
Surface preparation (grinding, degreasing) of the crack alignment;
•
Installation of surface ports at approximately 12-inch centers;
•
Low-pressure injection of hydrophobic polyurethane resin to refusal;
•
Removal of ports and grinding of surface residue flush with slab;
•
Cleanup and disposal of consumables.

additional cracks or joints outside the 40 lf treated length; work outside Zone

(surface water pumped down) at start of each shift
Unit rate applies for reconciliation if the finally-treated length differs from the 40 lf basis; commercial terms
otherwise as stated.

exit_code=0
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""AHPELE requirement scanner (stdlib only; runs inside the task container).

Finds requirement-like statements in the text corpus written by
ahpele_index.py (/tmp/ahpele/corpus) so that hard constraints are not missed:

  python3 ahpele_reqscan.py            # scan: writes /tmp/ahpele/req_candidates.md and .csv
  python3 ahpele_reqscan.py --check    # coverage: lists candidates not yet reviewed
  python3 ahpele_reqscan.py --register FILE.csv|.xlsx   # register rows: is each value in the document it cites?

A candidate counts as reviewed when its ID (e.g. R0042) appears in
/tmp/ahpele/requirements.csv (adopted) or /tmp/ahpele/rejected.csv (rejected,
with a reason). A whole document can be rejected by putting its path in
rejected.csv. The scanner is a recall aid: it misses requirements that live in
tables, drawings or images, and it lists many statements that are not hard
requirements. It knows nothing about any particular task.
"""
import argparse
import csv
import html
import json
import os
import re
import sys

OUT = "/tmp/ahpele"
STRONG = re.compile(
    r"\b(shall|must|is required|are required|required to|mandatory|not permitted|prohibited|shall not|"
    r"must not|may not exceed|no later than|condition of|subject to|is to|are to|(is|are)? ?limited to|"
    r"not (be )?(less|more|greater|lower|higher) than|not exceed|at least|at most|no more than|no less than|"
    r"maximum of|minimum of|is not allowed|are not allowed|will not be accepted|not acceptable)\b", re.I)
LIMIT = re.compile(
    r"(\b(not (to )?exceed|exceed(s|ing)?|maximum|minimum|max\.?|min\.?|at least|at most|no more than|"
    r"no less than|not less than|not more than|not greater than|up to|limit(ed|s)?|cap(ped)?|allowable|"
    r"permissible|permitted|threshold|tolerance|deadline|before|prior to|within|until|expires?|valid)\b|"
    r"[≤≥<>]=?|±|\+/-)", re.I)
NUMBER = re.compile(r"(?<![A-Za-z])[-+]?\d[\d,]*(?:\.\d+)?")
NOISE = re.compile(r"^(--- page \d+ ---|page \d+( of \d+)?|\W*)$", re.I)
MAX_LEN = 320
TAG = re.compile(r"<[^<>]{1,400}>")
# folders that usually hold general reference material (codes, standards, catalogues) rather than project documents
REFERENCE = re.compile(r"(^|/)(library|libraries|reference|references|standards?|codes?|regulations?|catalogues?|"
                       r"catalogs?|vendor|manufacturer)(/|$)", re.I)
# file names of published codes and standards (general engineering knowledge, not task-specific)
STANDARD_NAME = re.compile(
    r"^(\d+[ _-]?CFR|UFC|UFGS|UFM|ASCE|SEI|ACI|AISC|AISI|SDI|SJI|IBC|IRC|IFC[ _-]?\d|IECC|IEC|IEEE|NFPA|NEC|NESC|ISO|EN|"
    r"BS|ASTM|ASHRAE|ASME|AWS|AWWA|API|ANSI|UL|CSA|DIN|AS|NZS|TIA|FM|NEMA|OSHA|EPA|FEMA|AASHTO|MUTCD|ICC|NCHRP|"
    r"USACE|EM[ _-]\d|ETL|DoD|IS)[ _-]?\d", re.I)
DATA_TYPES = {"csv", "json"}
VOID_DIR = re.compile(r"(^|/)(archive[sd]?|superseded|obsolete|old|void|withdrawn|cancell?ed)(/|$)", re.I)


def load_inventory():
    try:
        with open(os.path.join(OUT, "inventory.json"), encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            return {r["path"]: r for r in json.load(fh).get("files", [])}
    except (OSError, ValueError):
        return {}


def statements(text):
    """Yield (page, statement) pairs: lines joined into sentences, table rows kept whole."""
    page, buf = 1, []
    for raw in text.splitlines():
        m = re.match(r"--- page (\d+) ---", raw.strip())
        if m:
            if buf:
                yield page, " ".join(buf)
                buf = []
            page = int(m.group(1))
            continue
        line = raw.strip()
        if NOISE.match(line):
            if buf:
                yield page, " ".join(buf)
                buf = []
            continue
        if "\t" in raw or " | " in line or line.count("  ") > 2:  # table-like row
            if buf:
                yield page, " ".join(buf)
                buf = []
            yield page, re.sub(r"\s+", " ", line)
            continue
        buf.append(line)
        if re.search(r"[.;:]$", line) or len(" ".join(buf)) > 600:
            yield page, " ".join(buf)
            buf = []
    if buf:
        yield page, " ".join(buf)


def split_sentences(s):
    parts = re.split(r"(?<=[.;])\s+(?=[A-Z(])", s)
    return [p.strip() for p in parts if p.strip()]


def scan():
    corpus = os.path.join(OUT, "corpus")
    inv = load_inventory()
    rows = []
    data_like = {d for d, r in inv.items() if r.get("type") in DATA_TYPES}
    for dp, _, fns in os.walk(corpus):
        for fn in sorted(fns):
            if not fn.endswith(".txt"):
                continue
            full = os.path.join(dp, fn)
            doc = os.path.relpath(full, corpus)[:-4]
            try:
                text = open(full, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
            except OSError:
                continue
            if text.count("<") > 20 and len(TAG.findall(text[:20000])) > 20:  # XML / HTML: keep the text only
                text = html.unescape(TAG.sub(lambda m: "\n" if re.match(r"</?(p|div|tr|li|h\d|head|br|section|para)\b",
                                                                     m.group(0), re.I) else " ", text))
            seen = set()
            for page, st in statements(text):
                for s in split_sentences(st):
                    strong, limit, nums = bool(STRONG.search(s)), bool(LIMIT.search(s)), NUMBER.findall(s)
                    if not (strong or (limit and nums)) or (doc in data_like and not strong):
                        continue
                    key = s.lower()[:200]
                    if key in seen or len(s) < 12:
                        continue
                    seen.add(key)
                    score = (4 if nums else 3) if strong else 2  # 4: modal + number, 3: modal, 2: limit + number
                    rows.append({"doc": doc, "page": page, "score": score,
                                 "text": s if len(s) <= MAX_LEN else s[:MAX_LEN] + "…",
                                 "numbers": " ".join(nums[:8])})
    for r in rows:
        r["ref"] = bool(REFERENCE.search(os.path.dirname(r["doc"]))
                        or STANDARD_NAME.search(os.path.basename(r["doc"])))
    rows.sort(key=lambda r: (r["ref"], r["doc"], r["page"]))
    for i, r in enumerate(rows, 1):
        r["id"] = f"R{i:04d}"
    with open(os.path.join(OUT, "req_candidates.csv"), "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        w = csv.DictWriter(fh, fieldnames=["id", "doc", "page", "score", "ref", "numbers", "text"])
        w.writeheader()
        w.writerows(rows)
    by_doc = {}
    for r in rows:
        by_doc.setdefault(r["doc"], []).append(r)
    lines = ["# Requirement candidates", "",
             f"{len(rows)} requirement-like statements in {len(by_doc)} documents (score 4: shall/must/"
             "not-more-than wording with a number; 3: the same wording without a number; 2: a limit word with a "
             "number, often context rather than a requirement). Tables, drawings and scanned pages are only partly covered: "
             "read those yourself. Status flags come from the FILE NAME; confirm which documents govern. Project "
             "documents come first; published codes and standards and documents in reference folders are listed "
             "last: the clauses that apply are the ones the project documents invoke. --check asks you to review the "
             "score 3-4 statements of project documents; use the rest when you look a requirement up.", ""]
    shown_ref = False
    for doc, rs in by_doc.items():
        if rs[0]["ref"] and not shown_ref:
            lines += ["# Reference folders (codes, standards, catalogues)", ""]
            shown_ref = True
        flags = inv.get(doc, {}).get("flags", "")
        lines.append(f"## {doc}" + (f"  [name flags: {flags}]" if flags else "") + f"  ({len(rs)})")
        for r in rs:
            lines.append(f"- {r['id']} p{r['page']} s{r['score']}: {r['text']}")
        lines.append("")
    with open(os.path.join(OUT, "req_candidates.md"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        fh.write("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
    key = [r for r in rows if must_review(r)]
    kdocs = {}
    for r in key:
        kdocs[r["doc"]] = kdocs.get(r["doc"], 0) + 1
    top = sorted(kdocs.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1])[:10]
    print(f"requirement scan: {len(rows)} candidates in {len(by_doc)} documents -> {OUT}/req_candidates.md; "
          f"{len(key)} strong candidates in project documents to review"
          + (" (" + ", ".join(f"{d}: {n}" for d, n in top) + ")" if top else ""))
    return rows


def must_review(r):
    """Requirement wording (shall, must, is to, not more than ...) in project documents."""
    return int(r["score"]) >= 3 and str(r["ref"]) not in ("True", "1")


def read_text(path):
    try:
        return open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
    except OSError:
        return ""


def check(limit):
    path = os.path.join(OUT, "req_candidates.csv")
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        scan()
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        rows = list(csv.DictReader(fh))
    adopted = read_text(os.path.join(OUT, "requirements.csv"))
    rejected = read_text(os.path.join(OUT, "rejected.csv"))
    if not adopted.strip():
        print(f"{OUT}/requirements.csv is missing or empty: build the requirements table first "
              "(one row per hard requirement, with the candidate IDs it comes from).")
    ids = set(re.findall(r"\bR\d{4}\b", adopted + "\n" + rejected))
    rejected_docs = {r["doc"] for r in rows if r["doc"] in rejected}
    inv = load_inventory()
    key = [r for r in rows if must_review(r)]

    def covered(r):
        if r["id"] in ids:
            return True
        if r["doc"] not in rejected_docs:
            return False
        # rejecting a whole document covers its statements with a number only when the document is marked void
        # (status word in its file name, or an archive / superseded folder); otherwise each one needs its own ID
        return int(r["score"]) < 4 or bool(inv.get(r["doc"], {}).get("flags")) or bool(VOID_DIR.search(r["doc"]))

    open_rows = [r for r in key if not covered(r)]
    open_rows.sort(key=lambda r: (-int(r["score"]), r["doc"], int(r["page"])))
    n = len(key)
    print(f"coverage: {n - len(open_rows)}/{n} strong project-document candidates reviewed "
          f"({len(ids & {r['id'] for r in rows})} IDs cited in all, {len(rejected_docs)} documents rejected whole); "
          f"{len(open_rows)} not reviewed yet. ({len(rows) - n} weaker or code/standard candidates are optional: "
          f"see {OUT}/req_candidates.md.)")
    if not open_rows:
        print("Every candidate is adopted or rejected. Also check tables, drawings and scanned pages, which the "
              "scanner does not fully cover.")
        return 0
    print("Unreviewed candidates, strongest first (add each hard requirement to requirements.csv citing its ID, or "
          "list the ID with a reason in rejected.csv; a statement with a number in a document that is not marked "
          "void needs its own ID even if you rejected the document):")
    for r in open_rows[:limit]:
        print(f"- {r['id']} [{r['doc']} p{r['page']} s{r['score']}] {r['text'][:220]}")
    if len(open_rows) > limit:
        by = {}
        for r in open_rows[limit:]:
            by[r["doc"]] = by.get(r["doc"], 0) + 1
        print(f"... and {len(open_rows) - limit} more: " + ", ".join(f"{d} ({c})" for d, c in sorted(by.items())))
    return 1


SRC_COL = re.compile(r"source|clause|document|doc\b|ref|citation|basis|standard|section", re.I)
VAL_COL = re.compile(r"value|limit|threshold|criterion|criteria|requirement|min|max|allow", re.I)
CLAUSE_REF = re.compile(r"(§\s*[\w.()-]+|\b(?:clause|section|sec\.|para\.?|table|article|art\.)\s*[\w.()-]+)", re.I)


def norm_num(x):
    x = x.replace(",", "")

[P8] 1.  PURPOSE
[P9] This memorandum records Thelbridge's verification of Item 048 on the Package A Review Comment and Verification Register. Item 048 is the delegated design of the temporary support of excavation (SOE) for the Block B plant-room excavation: Kesterline Submittal 31-SH-B Rev.1, sealed 06/11/2026, as supplemented by Revision 2 under letter KE-L-2026-0713, dated and sealed 07/13/2026. The excavation is 24 ft deep, from working grade El. 750.0 to plant-room subgrade El. 726.0, and is scheduled to start on 08/10/2026.
[P10] The determination is NOT VERIFIED. The current revision cannot be relied on for the excavation. Item 048 remains Open and the 08/10/2026 start is not released. The design's groundwater and stratigraphic values are correct, but its engineered-fill unit weight and undrained shear strength are not supported by the record; the toe-embedment, anchor-bond, sheet-pile flexure and wall-deflection checks fail on record inputs; the base-heave check passes only at the controlled head and fails at the design's own 727.0 ft stop-work trigger or with 0.5 ft of overdig; and the separately sealed Block B dewatering plan and the interface with the completed Block B mat, piles and K-5 joint are missing. Section 5 sets out what must be produced, by whom, and what this means for 08/10/2026.
[P12] 2.  DOCUMENTS REVIEWED
[P13] The review was made against the following record. Revisions and dates are as stated in the documents. Where a document has been superseded in whole or in part, the governing part is identified.
[P14] Documents reviewed but not relied on: Rev.1 Section 2 and Section 3.4 dry-excavation assumption (withdrawn by Rev.2 R2.1); 31-DW-A Block A well-point details (outside Block B); Calculation CB-GEO-004 (pile design, Item 049) and CB-STR-011 (mat design, Item 050), used only for interface checks; Sheet S-310/CB-STR-018 (podium, Item 055). The Rev.2 supplement is not entered in the Submittal Register; 31-SH-B Rev.1 is recorded as "Under review" as of 07/13/2026.
[P16] 3.  BASIS OF REVIEW
[P17] Precedence. DBM §1 states that the DBM governs all Package A calculations and controls subordinate documents; DBM §9 states that the GIR remains controlling for all soil parameters and any conflict is resolved in favour of the GIR. The GIR Rev.2 is therefore the governing source for groundwater, stratigraphy and soil strength. Rev.2's supersession matrix is applied only to the sections it expressly supersedes; sections left in force are checked for consistency with the new loads and geometry. RFI 104 and A-501 Rev.3 govern the permitted wall-to-mat joints; Spec 31 20 00 Articles 3.4.B and 3.6 govern fill acceptance and settlement; 31-DW-A Articles 1.2 and 4.2 govern the scope of dewatering. Where a requirement can be read two ways, the stricter reading is applied: the GIR upper-bound su of 1,100 psf, the record fill density, and a controlled head of 726.5 ft rather than the 727.0 ft trigger.
[P18] Table 3-1 — Governing parameters applied
[P19] Table 3-2 — Acceptance criteria applied
[P20] Method. The reviewer independently recomputed the active pressure (layered effective stress with hydrostatic water), passive resistance (total stress, su), free-earth toe moment, anchor force and bond, sheet-pile bending, wall deflection, base heave and dewatering consolidation. The designer's arithmetic was reproduced where the inputs are the same; differences are identified. The record fill unit weight is derived from the accepted fill: 95% of the Proctor maximum dry density 128.4 pcf, at the 9.2% optimum moisture, gives γtotal = 0.95 × 128.4 × 1.092 = 133.2 pcf (132.0 to 135.6 pcf over the permitted moisture window). The GIR su range of 900 to 1,100 psf is used; 1,100 psf is the upper bound and therefore the least conservative record value. The design's 1,400 psf is not supported by the GIR or the index data.
[P22] 4.  FINDINGS
[P23] Finding 1 — Current revision and document status
[P24] Rev.2 is sealed and signed by B. A. Halvard, PE (Ohio P.E. No. E-58730, expires 12/31/2027) on 07/13/2026, so it is a valid later revision to the extent it supersedes Rev.1. However, the supersession matrix leaves Rev.1 Sections 1, 2, 3.1–3.3, 4.1, 4.2, 8, 11.3, 11.4, 12 and 13 in force. Three of those are inconsistent with Rev.2: (a) Section 2 still records the dry-excavation assumption of 31-DW-A, which Rev.2 Section 1 withdraws; (b) Section 11.3 still specifies a 28-ft PZ-35 single mill length, while Rev.2 R2.4 uses 30.5-ft sheets to tip El. 719.5; (c) Section 8's overturning and sliding checks use the Rev.1 loads (17,844 lb/ft) and toe El. 722.0, not the Rev.2 loads (19,610 lb/ft) and toe El. 719.5. In addition, the Rev.2 supplement is not logged in the Submittal Register (31-SH-B Rev.1 remains "Under review" as of 07/13/2026), and the Rev.1 Section 13 shoring drawings are not in the review file. The package is therefore not a complete, internally consistent design even before the numerical checks.
[P25] Finding 2 — Groundwater and stratigraphy are correctly stated
[P26] The GIR, the 19-round boring-log/monitoring record through 06/28/2026 and the Field Observation Report confirm the design water table El. 742.0 (range El. 741.6–742.4), the confined head El. 738.0 (range El. 737.7–738.3), the top of the confined aquifer El. 720.0, and the clay aquitard El. 738.0–720.0 (18 ft, 120 pcf). Borings B-04 and B-06 are inside the plant-room footprint and confirm the clay top and base. There is no evidence of a higher water table or a perched surface that would change the design groundwater. The groundwater values in Rev.2 are therefore verified and can be carried forward. What is not verified is the design's response: Rev.2 introduces active depressurization to El. 726.5 (11.5 ft of drawdown), whereas 31-DW-A Rev.1 and register Item 006 record a Block B cutoff wall toed at El. 722.0 with no active drawdown. That is a change of strategy, not a groundwater reading.
[P27] Finding 3 — The engineered-fill unit weight is understated (118 pcf vs 133.2 pcf)
[P28] Rev.2 uses 118 pcf for the 12 ft of engineered fill from El. 750.0 to El. 738.0 (R2.3). That is the GIR design unit weight for the upper sand, not for the compacted structural fill. The fill record RB-FPR-BB-2025 records 14 lifts, 12 ft, at 95% of the Proctor maximum 128.4 pcf and 9.2% optimum moisture. The corresponding total unit weight is 0.95 × 128.4 × 1.092 = 133.2 pcf (132.0–135.6 pcf over the permitted moisture window). Using 118 pcf understates the retained fill weight by about 11%.
[P29] Table 4-1 — Active lateral load, Rev.2 inputs vs record fill
[P30] The reviewer's layered integration reproduces the R2.3 load of 19,610 lb/ft but gives a driving moment of 227,532 ft-lb/ft, 4.1% below the 237,293 ft-lb/ft stated in R2.3; the designer's moment arm is conservative. The difference does not change any conclusion. The significant effect of the fill unit weight is on the passive resistance: even retaining the designer's su of 1,400 psf, the toe factor of safety falls from 1.62 (reviewer's reproduction) or 1.55 (Rev.2) to 1.43, below the required 1.50. The fill unit weight alone therefore fails the toe check; it also understates the anchor demand, flexure and deflection.
[P31] Finding 4 — The undrained shear strength is not supported by the GIR (1,400 psf vs 900–1,100 psf)
[P32] Rev.1 §3.2 and Rev.2 R2.4 use su = 1,400 psf. GIR §6.3 reports su = 900–1,100 psf from field vane and unconsolidated-undrained triaxial testing; the index and consolidation data contain no 1,400 psf value. DBM §9 makes the GIR controlling for soil parameters. A 1,400 psf value would require site-specific testing and a sealed geotechnical confirmation, neither of which is in the record. Applying the upper bound of the logged range (1,100 psf) is the least conservative record-based value.
[P33] With record fill and su 1,100 psf: pn = 4(1,100) − 3,288 = 1,112 psf (vs 2,494 psf design); Pp = 1,112 × 6.5 = 7,225 lb/ft (vs 16,211); MR = 7,225 × 22.75 = 164,374 ft-lb/ft (vs 368,800); toe FS = 164,374 / 239,786 = 0.69. At su 900 psf, FS = 0.19. The required embedment at record inputs is about 12.6 ft (tip about El. 713.4) if clay passive is used over the full depth; the design provides 6.5 ft. The 1,400 psf value is the single largest non-conservative input in the design.
[P34] Finding 5 — Toe embedment fails on record inputs
[P35] Table 4-2 — Toe embedment factor of safety (criterion FS ≥ 1.50; D = 6.5 ft, tip El. 719.5)
[P36] Only the designer's 118 pcf / 1,400 psf case passes. Neither input is supported by the record. The toe check cannot be carried forward. A revised design must either increase the embedment (about 12.6 ft at record inputs, tip about El. 713.4, which penetrates the aquifer), add a second anchor level, or otherwise reduce the load. The current tip El. 719.5 is 0.5 ft into the aquifer; the design states that the sheet is not a cutoff and relies on the relief wells, but GIR §9.6 requires every penetration of the clay to be sealed at the aquitard. No interlock seal detail is in the record. The 30.5-ft sheet also conflicts with Rev.1 §11.3's 28-ft sheet (Finding 1).
[P37] Finding 6 — The anchor bond zone is in clay, not dense sand and gravel; bond and proof test fail
[P38] The anchor is at El. 745.5, inclined 20° below horizontal, with 25 ft free length and 24 ft bond length (49 ft total). At 20° the anchor tip is at El. 745.5 − 49 sin 20° = El. 728.74. The bond zone runs from El. 736.95 to El. 728.74, entirely within the CL clay (El. 738.0–720.0). It does not reach the dense sand and gravel below El. 720.0; to do so would require (745.5 − 720.0)/sin 20° = 74.6 ft total. The 20 psi bond stress used in R2.5 is the FHWA-IF-99-015 Table 4 value for dense sand and gravel; it is not applicable to the clay actually penetrated. At the stiff-clay end of the same table (10 psi), the 24-ft bond gives Q = π × 0.5 × 24 × 10 × 144 = 54.3 kips, below the Rev.2 design load of 56.2 kips and far below the record design load of 102.0 kips.
[P39] Table 4-3 — Anchor demand, bond capacity and proof test (6 ft spacing, 20°; 24-ft bond, 6-in diameter)
[P40] Even if the bond were in sand, the record-fill / 1,100 psf demand gives FS 1.06 at 20 psi, below the 2.0 normally required for temporary ground anchors under FHWA-IF-99-015; the proof test of 135.7 kips exceeds the 108.6-kip bond capacity, so the anchor cannot be proof-tested to 1.33 × design. The 49-ft anchors extend about 46 ft horizontally from the wall at El. 745.5, under the existing mat and across the 48-pile group; no clash or clearance check is in the record. RFI 048 only addresses 6-in clear to wall reinforcement. The anchor design cannot be carried forward.
[P41] Finding 7 — Sheet-pile flexure fails on record inputs
[P42] With Rev.2 inputs, Mmax = 62.4 kip-ft/ft at El. 733.1, Mallow = 121 kip-ft/ft and FS = 1.94; the reviewer reproduces 62.45 kip-ft/ft. With record fill and su 1,400 psf, Mmax rises to 83.8 kip-ft/ft (FS 1.45, below 1.5); with record fill and su 1,100 psf, Mmax is 162.4 kip-ft/ft (FS 0.75) and exceeds the allowable moment. The flexure check fails on record inputs and cannot be carried forward. Table 4-4 summarises this and the deflection check.
[P43] Table 4-4 — Flexure and deflection
[P44] Finding 8 — Wall deflection exceeds H/200
[P45] Rev.2 predicts 1.3 in at El. 738.0 against H/200 = 1.44 in, a margin of only 0.14 in. Scaling the designer's own method by the increase in maximum moment gives about 1.74 in for record fill and su 1,400 psf, and about 3.4 in for record fill and su 1,100 psf, both above 1.44 in. The method is not independently reproducible from the record (no soil modulus or stiffness is stated), so the check is not verified; a revised deflection analysis is required. The deflection check cannot be carried forward.
[P46] Finding 9 — Base heave passes only at the controlled point; the operating envelope fails
[P47] The arithmetic is correct: W = 6.0 × 120 = 720 psf; 0.9W = 648 psf; at the controlled head El. 726.5, u = (726.5 − 720.0) × 62.4 = 405.6 psf; FS = 648 / 405.6 = 1.60, above 1.50. But the operating envelope is not. At the R2.7 stop-work trigger El. 727.0, u = 436.8 psf and FS = 1.48, below 1.50. If the plug is 5.5 ft (0.5 ft of overdig), FS at 726.5 is 1.46 and at 727.0 is 1.36. At the initial head El. 738.0, FS is 0.58. The design has only a 6.7% margin at the controlled point, and its own trigger permits non-compliance. Pumping is the sole safeguard; there is no standby pump or power, automatic alarm, or response plan in the record.
[P48] Table 4-5 — Base-heave factor of safety vs head and plug thickness (criterion FS ≥ 1.50)
[P49] The base-heave formula can be carried forward only with the following conditions: stop-work trigger at or below El. 726.5 (preferably 726.0), no excavation below El. 726.0, continuous pumping with standby pumps and standby power, automatic high-head alarm, and a permanent plant-room slab designed for the full confined head El. 738.0. As written, the check is not verified.
[P50] Finding 10 — Global stability and overturning are stale and not updated for Rev.2
[P51] Rev.1 §8 remains in force under the Rev.2 matrix but was not updated. Its FS 2.06 uses the Rev.1 loads (17,844 lb/ft), passive 2,490 lb/ft and toe El. 722.0; none of these apply to Rev.2 (19,610 lb/ft, allowable passive 10,807 lb/ft, toe El. 719.5). Recomputing the §8.2 check on the Rev.2 geometry gives FS 0.94 for the designer's inputs, 1.04 for record fill and su 1,400 psf, and 1.43 for record fill and su 1,100 psf, not 2.06. The §8.1 "wall-free" sliding FS of 0.28 is not a design check with the tieback. The global stability section must be reissued. The design also does not check lateral support to the existing mat and piles, excavation unloading and heave, or vibration; those are addressed in Findings 11 and 12.
[P52] Finding 11 — The Block B dewatering plan is missing, and the excavation affects permanent work already built
[P53] 31-DW-A Rev.1 Article 1.2 expressly limits the plan to Block A and says the Block B plant-room will be addressed by a separate delegated design; Article 4.2 says the plan shall not be relied on for any design that assumes a reduction in the confined head below El. 738.0. It gives four 8-in relief wells and a target head, but no pumping rate, well hydraulics or radius of influence, discharge permit (NPDES), standby pump or power, monitoring frequency, contingency, or well decommissioning. The concept is not a complete dewatering design.
[P54] Effects on the permanent work already built at Block B:
[P55] •  Clay consolidation and downdrag. Drawdown from El. 738.0 to 726.5 increases the effective stress at the base of the clay by 11.5 × 62.4 = 717.6 psf, an average of about 359 psf over the 18-ft layer. With Cc 0.28, e0 0.92, H 18 ft and σ′0 1,850 psf, the ultimate consolidation is about 1.9 in on the record fill (about 2.4 in using the GIR mid-layer σ′0). About 0.6 in develops in 6 months and 0.9 in in 12 months. This is the same order as, or exceeds, the Spec 31 20 00 Article 3.6 total tolerance of 1.0 in; the differential component must be evaluated by the EOR.
[P56] •  Pile downdrag. Using the pile design's α = 0.55 and the GIR su of 1,100 psf over the 18-ft clay, the dewatering-induced downdrag is about 45.6 kips per 16-in pile (perimeter 4.19 ft × 18 ft × 0.55 × 1,100 psf). The pile allowable is 240 kips and the service load 180 kips, a 60-kip margin; utilisation rises from 0.75 to about 0.94 before any other effect. Calculation CB-GEO-004 (Item 049) did not include this drawdown case; the EOR must check it.
[P57] •  Mat edge, lateral support and heave. The 24-ft excavation removes about (12 × 133.2 + 12 × 120) × 2,992 sf ≈ 9,090 kips of overburden over the 68 × 44 ft pit. The resulting heave/rebound and lateral relief at the adjacent mat edge and piles are not checked; the shoring design treats the pit as a free perimeter. The mat is pile-supported, but its edge at the plant-room boundary loses lateral support and the clay beneath it will move.
[P58] •  Waterproofing and the K-5 joint. K-5 at grid K/5 is at the plant-room boundary (S-102 Rev.2; A-501 Rev.3). It uses Detail 1 positive-side bentonite membrane with a hydrophilic waterstop, rated to 20 ft head. The plant-room excavation is on the positive side; the membrane and waterstop may be exposed, damaged or reversed. The AOR/EOR must provide a plant-room boundary waterproofing detail and an inspection hold point. The design cannot be constructed as shown without a boundary section and a revised sequence.
