THELBRIDGE PROJECT MANAGEMENT SERVICES
500 South High Street, Suite 720, Columbus, OH 43215  |  (614) 555-0125  |  thelbridgepm.com
VERIFICATION MEMORANDUM
To:	Rachel Marlbeck, University Program Director, Thornbury State University
From:	Adrian Vance, Project Engineer (Structural/Geotechnical), Thelbridge Project Management Services, Owner's Representative
Date:	July 20, 2026
Subject:	Item 048 — Block B Plant-Room Shoring: Verification of Kesterline Submittal 31-SH-B Rev.1 (sealed 06/11/2026) as supplemented by Rev.2 (KE-L-2026-0713, sealed 07/13/2026) — NOT VERIFIED
cc:  Steven Kendrow, Rowan Bay Constructors, Inc.; Gregory Nash, PE, Calloway Braddock Structural Engineers, LLC; Rahul Nimkar, Thelbridge Project Management Services (Geotechnical Reviewer); Project File
1.  PURPOSE
This memorandum records Thelbridge's verification of Item 048 on the Package A Review Comment and Verification Register. Item 048 is the delegated design of the temporary support of excavation (SOE) for the Block B plant-room excavation: Kesterline Submittal 31-SH-B Rev.1, sealed 06/11/2026, as supplemented by Revision 2 under letter KE-L-2026-0713, dated and sealed 07/13/2026. The excavation is 24 ft deep, from working grade El. 750.0 to plant-room subgrade El. 726.0, and is scheduled to start on 08/10/2026.
The determination is NOT VERIFIED. The current revision cannot be relied on for the excavation. Item 048 remains Open and the 08/10/2026 start is not released. The design's groundwater and stratigraphic values are correct, but its engineered-fill unit weight and undrained shear strength are not supported by the record; the toe-embedment, anchor-bond, sheet-pile flexure and wall-deflection checks fail on record inputs; the base-heave check passes only at the controlled head and fails at the design's own 727.0 ft stop-work trigger or with 0.5 ft of overdig; and the separately sealed Block B dewatering plan and the interface with the completed Block B mat, piles and K-5 joint are missing. Section 5 sets out what must be produced, by whom, and what this means for 08/10/2026.
2.  DOCUMENTS REVIEWED
The review was made against the following record. Revisions and dates are as stated in the documents. Where a document has been superseded in whole or in part, the governing part is identified.
Documents reviewed but not relied on: Rev.1 Section 2 and Section 3.4 dry-excavation assumption (Section 3.4 is superseded by Rev.2 R2.1; Section 2 remains in force but is contradicted by R2.1); 31-DW-A Block A well-point details (outside Block B); Calculation CB-GEO-004 (pile design, Item 049) and CB-STR-011 (mat design, Item 050), used only for interface checks; Sheet S-310/CB-STR-018 (podium, Item 055). The Rev.2 supplement is not entered in the Submittal Register; 31-SH-B Rev.1 is recorded as "Under review" as of 07/13/2026. All documents cited in Table 2-1 are the current revisions in the project record: GIR Rev.2 supersedes GIR Rev.1; DBM Rev.2 supersedes DBM Rev.1; Spec 31 20 00 Rev.3 supersedes Rev.2; S-101/S-201 Rev.4 supersede prior issues; A-501 Rev.3 supersedes prior revisions. Rev.1 of 31-SH-B is used only for the sections Rev.2 leaves in force, as identified in Finding 1.
3.  BASIS OF REVIEW
Precedence. DBM §1 states that the DBM governs all Package A calculations and controls subordinate documents; DBM §9 states that the GIR remains controlling for all soil parameters and any conflict is resolved in favour of the GIR. The GIR Rev.2 is therefore the governing source for groundwater, stratigraphy and soil strength. Rev.2's supersession matrix is applied only to the sections it expressly supersedes; sections left in force are checked for consistency with the new loads and geometry. RFI 104 and A-501 Rev.3 govern the permitted wall-to-mat joints; Spec 31 20 00 Articles 3.4.B and 3.6 govern fill acceptance and settlement; 31-DW-A Articles 1.2 and 4.2 govern the scope of dewatering. Where a requirement can be read two ways, the stricter reading is applied: the GIR upper-bound su of 1,100 psf, the record fill density, and a controlled head of 726.5 ft rather than the 727.0 ft trigger.
Table 3-1 — Governing parameters applied
Table 3-2 — Acceptance criteria applied
Method. The reviewer independently recomputed the active pressure (layered effective stress with hydrostatic water), passive resistance (total stress, su), free-earth toe moment, anchor force and bond, sheet-pile bending, wall deflection, base heave and dewatering consolidation. The designer's arithmetic was reproduced where the inputs are the same; differences are identified. The record fill unit weight is derived from the accepted fill: 95% of the Proctor maximum dry density 128.4 pcf, at the 9.2% optimum moisture, gives γtotal = 0.95 × 128.4 × 1.092 = 133.2 pcf (132.0 to 135.6 pcf over the permitted moisture window). The GIR su range of 900 to 1,100 psf is used; 1,100 psf is the upper bound and therefore the least conservative record value. The design's 1,400 psf is not supported by the GIR or the index data.
4.  FINDINGS
Finding 1 — Current revision and document status
Rev.2 is sealed and signed by B. A. Halvard, PE (Ohio P.E. No. E-58730, expires 12/31/2027) on 07/13/2026, so it is a valid later revision to the extent it supersedes Rev.1. However, the supersession matrix leaves Rev.1 Sections 1, 2, 3.1–3.3, 4.1, 4.2, 8, 11.3, 11.4, 12 and 13 in force. Four of those are inconsistent with Rev.2: (a) Section 2 still records the dry-excavation assumption of 31-DW-A, which Rev.2 Section 1 withdraws; (b) Section 11.3 still specifies a 28-ft PZ-35 single mill length, while Rev.2 R2.4 uses 30.5-ft sheets to tip El. 719.5; (c) Section 8's overturning and sliding checks use the Rev.1 loads (17,844 lb/ft) and toe El. 722.0, not the Rev.2 loads (19,610 lb/ft) and toe El. 719.5; (d) Section 13.1 item 2 still starts the Block A dewatering system (31-DW-A) 14 days before excavation, whereas Rev.2 relies on the Block B relief wells. In addition, the Rev.2 supplement is not logged in the Submittal Register (31-SH-B Rev.1 remains "Under review" as of 07/13/2026), and the Rev.1 Section 13 shoring drawings are not in the review file. The package is therefore not a complete, internally consistent design even before the numerical checks.
Finding 2 — Groundwater and stratigraphy are correctly stated
The GIR, the 19-round boring-log/monitoring record through 06/28/2026 and the Field Observation Report confirm the design water table El. 742.0 (range El. 741.6–742.4), the confined head El. 738.0 (range El. 737.7–738.3), the top of the confined aquifer El. 720.0, and the clay aquitard El. 738.0–720.0 (18 ft, 120 pcf). Borings B-04 and B-06 are inside the plant-room footprint and confirm the clay top and base. There is no evidence of a higher water table or a perched surface that would change the design groundwater. The groundwater values in Rev.2 are therefore verified and can be carried forward. What is not verified is the design's response: Rev.2 introduces active depressurization to El. 726.5 (11.5 ft of drawdown), whereas 31-DW-A Rev.1 and register Item 006 record a Block B cutoff wall toed at El. 722.0 with no active drawdown. That is a change of strategy, not a groundwater reading.
Finding 3 — The engineered-fill unit weight is understated (118 pcf vs 133.2 pcf)
Rev.2 uses 118 pcf for the 12 ft of engineered fill from El. 750.0 to El. 738.0 (R2.3). That is the GIR design unit weight for the upper sand, not for the compacted structural fill. The fill record RB-FPR-BB-2025 records 14 lifts, 12 ft, at 95% of the Proctor maximum 128.4 pcf and 9.2% optimum moisture. The corresponding total unit weight is 0.95 × 128.4 × 1.092 = 133.2 pcf (132.0–135.6 pcf over the permitted moisture window). Using 118 pcf understates the retained fill weight by about 11%.
Table 4-1 — Active lateral load, Rev.2 inputs vs record fill
The reviewer's layered integration reproduces the R2.3 load of 19,610 lb/ft but gives a driving moment of 227,532 ft-lb/ft, 4.1% below the 237,293 ft-lb/ft stated in R2.3; the designer's moment arm is conservative. The record fill increases the total horizontal load by 6.1% and reduces pn by 7.3% even at su 1,400 psf; the larger effect is the 5.9% increase in σv. The significant effect of the fill unit weight is on the passive resistance: even retaining the designer's su of 1,400 psf, the toe factor of safety falls from 1.62 (reviewer's reproduction) or 1.55 (Rev.2) to 1.43, below the required 1.50. The fill unit weight alone therefore fails the toe check; it also understates the anchor demand, flexure and deflection.
Finding 4 — The undrained shear strength is not supported by the GIR (1,400 psf vs 900–1,100 psf)
Rev.1 §3.2 and Rev.2 R2.4 use su = 1,400 psf. GIR §6.3 reports su = 900–1,100 psf from field vane and unconsolidated-undrained triaxial testing; the index and consolidation data contain no 1,400 psf value. DBM §9 makes the GIR controlling for soil parameters. A 1,400 psf value would require site-specific testing and a sealed geotechnical confirmation, neither of which is in the record. The reviewer notes that Calculation CB-GEO-004 uses an average su of 1,820 psf for pile shaft adhesion; that value is also outside the GIR range and is a separate inconsistency to be resolved under Item 049, but it cannot support the shoring value. Applying the upper bound of the logged range (1,100 psf) is the least conservative record-based value.
With record fill and su 1,100 psf: pn = 4(1,100) − 3,288 = 1,112 psf (vs 2,494 psf design); Pp = 1,112 × 6.5 = 7,225 lb/ft (vs 16,211); MR = 7,225 × 22.75 = 164,374 ft-lb/ft (vs 368,800); toe FS = 164,374 / 239,786 = 0.69. At su 900 psf, FS = 0.19. The required embedment at record inputs is about 12.6 ft (tip about El. 713.4) if clay passive is used over the full depth; the design provides 6.5 ft. The 1,400 psf value is the single largest non-conservative input in the design.
Finding 5 — Toe embedment fails on record inputs
Table 4-2 — Toe embedment factor of safety (criterion FS ≥ 1.50; D = 6.5 ft, tip El. 719.5)
Only the designer's 118 pcf / 1,400 psf case passes. Neither input is supported by the record. The toe check cannot be carried forward. A revised design must either increase the embedment (about 12.6 ft at record inputs, tip about El. 713.4, which penetrates the aquifer), add a second anchor level, or otherwise reduce the load. The current tip El. 719.5 is 0.5 ft into the aquifer; the design states that the sheet is not a cutoff and relies on the relief wells, but GIR §9.6 requires every penetration of the clay to be sealed at the aquitard. No interlock seal detail is in the record, and no seepage or piping check at the toe or along the sheet-soil interface is included. The 30.5-ft sheet also conflicts with Rev.1 §11.3's 28-ft sheet (Finding 1).
Finding 6 — The anchor bond zone is in clay, not dense sand and gravel; bond and proof test fail
The anchor is at El. 745.5, inclined 20° below horizontal, with 25 ft free length and 24 ft bond length (49 ft total). At 20° the anchor tip is at El. 745.5 − 49 sin 20° = El. 728.74. The bond zone runs from El. 736.95 to El. 728.74, entirely within the CL clay (El. 738.0–720.0). It does not reach the dense sand and gravel below El. 720.0; to do so would require (745.5 − 720.0)/sin 20° = 74.6 ft total. The 20 psi bond stress used in R2.5 is the FHWA-IF-99-015 Table 4 value for dense sand and gravel; it is not applicable to the clay actually penetrated. At the stiff-clay end of the same table (10 psi), the 24-ft bond gives Q = π × 0.5 × 24 × 10 × 144 = 54.3 kips, below the Rev.2 design load of 56.2 kips and far below the record design load of 102.0 kips.
Table 4-3 — Anchor demand, bond capacity and proof test (6 ft spacing, 20°; 24-ft bond, 6-in diameter)
Even if the bond were in sand, the record-fill / 1,100 psf demand gives FS 1.06 at 20 psi, below the 2.0 normally required for temporary ground anchors under FHWA-IF-99-015; the proof test of 135.7 kips exceeds the 108.6-kip bond capacity, so the anchor cannot be proof-tested to 1.33 × design. On the mat sides, the 49-ft anchors extend about 46 ft horizontally from the wall at El. 745.5, beneath the existing mat and across the 48-pile group; no clash or clearance check is in the record. RFI 048 only addresses 6-in clear to wall reinforcement. The anchor design cannot be carried forward.
Finding 7 — Sheet-pile flexure fails on record inputs
With Rev.2 inputs, Mmax = 62.4 kip-ft/ft at El. 733.1, Mallow = 121 kip-ft/ft and FS = 1.94; the reviewer reproduces 62.45 kip-ft/ft. With record fill and su 1,400 psf, Mmax rises to 83.8 kip-ft/ft (FS 1.45, below 1.5); with record fill and su 1,100 psf, Mmax is 162.4 kip-ft/ft (FS 0.75) and exceeds the allowable moment. The flexure check fails on record inputs and cannot be carried forward. Table 4-4 summarises this and the deflection check.
Table 4-4 — Flexure and deflection
Finding 8 — Wall deflection exceeds H/200
Rev.2 predicts 1.3 in at El. 738.0 against H/200 = 1.44 in, a margin of only 0.14 in. Scaling the designer's own method by the increase in maximum moment gives about 1.74 in for record fill and su 1,400 psf, and about 3.4 in for record fill and su 1,100 psf, both above 1.44 in. The method is not independently reproducible from the record (no soil modulus or stiffness is stated), so the check is not verified; a revised deflection analysis is required. The deflection check cannot be carried forward.
Finding 9 — Base heave passes only at the controlled point; the operating envelope fails
The arithmetic is correct: W = 6.0 × 120 = 720 psf; 0.9W = 648 psf; at the controlled head El. 726.5, u = (726.5 − 720.0) × 62.4 = 405.6 psf; FS = 648 / 405.6 = 1.60, above 1.50. But the operating envelope is not. At the R2.7 stop-work trigger El. 727.0, u = 436.8 psf and FS = 1.48, below 1.50. If the plug is 5.5 ft (0.5 ft of overdig), FS at 726.5 is 1.46 and at 727.0 is 1.36. At the initial head El. 738.0, FS is 0.58. The design has only a 6.7% margin at the controlled point, and its own trigger permits non-compliance. Pumping is the sole safeguard; there is no standby pump or power, automatic alarm, or response plan in the record.
Table 4-5 — Base-heave factor of safety vs head and plug thickness (criterion FS ≥ 1.50)
The base-heave formula can be carried forward only with the following conditions: stop-work trigger at or below El. 726.5 (preferably 726.0), no excavation below El. 726.0, continuous pumping with standby pumps and standby power, automatic high-head alarm, and a permanent plant-room slab designed for the full confined head El. 738.0. As written, the check is not verified.
Finding 10 — Global stability and overturning are stale and not updated for Rev.2
Rev.1 §8 remains in force under the Rev.2 matrix but was not updated. Its FS 2.06 uses the Rev.1 loads (17,844 lb/ft), passive 2,490 lb/ft and toe El. 722.0; none of these apply to Rev.2 (19,610 lb/ft, allowable passive 10,807 lb/ft, toe El. 719.5). Recomputing the §8.2 check on the Rev.2 geometry gives FS 0.94 for the designer's inputs, 1.04 for record fill and su 1,400 psf, and 1.43 for record fill and su 1,100 psf, not 2.06. That is an indicator that §8 was not updated, not a separate free-earth check; §8.2 treats the tieback reaction as an external resisting force, whereas R2.4 uses the free-earth formulation. The §8.1 "wall-free" sliding FS of 0.28 is not a design check with the tieback. The global stability section must be reissued. The design also does not check lateral support to the existing mat and piles, excavation unloading and heave, or vibration; those are addressed in Findings 11 and 12.
Finding 11 — The Block B dewatering plan is missing, and the excavation affects permanent work already built
31-DW-A Rev.1 Article 1.2 expressly limits the plan to Block A and says the Block B plant-room will be addressed by a separate delegated design; Article 4.2 says the plan shall not be relied on for any design that assumes a reduction in the confined head below El. 738.0. Rev.2 introduces exactly such a reduction (to El. 726.5) but is a shoring supplement, not the separately sealed dewatering and hydrogeologic analysis 31-DW-A requires. It gives four 8-in relief wells and a target head, but no pumping rate, well hydraulics or radius of influence, discharge permit (NPDES), standby pump or power, monitoring frequency, contingency, or well decommissioning. The concept is not a complete dewatering design. The June 2026 Monthly Progress Report records CO-19 for Block B dewatering as a pending change order, not executed; the dewatering scope and responsibility must be authorised before the work.
Effects on the permanent work already built at Block B:
•  Clay consolidation and downdrag. Drawdown from El. 738.0 to 726.5 increases the effective stress at the base of the clay by 11.5 × 62.4 = 717.6 psf, an average of about 359 psf over the 18-ft layer. With Cc 0.28, e0 0.92, H 18 ft and σ′0 1,850 psf, the ultimate consolidation is about 1.9 in on the record fill (about 2.4 in using the GIR mid-layer σ′0). About 0.6 in develops in 6 months and 0.9 in in 12 months. This is the same order as, or exceeds, the Spec 31 20 00 Article 3.6 total tolerance of 1.0 in; the differential component must be evaluated by the EOR.
•  Pile downdrag. Using the pile design's α = 0.55 and the GIR su of 1,100 psf over the 18-ft clay, the dewatering-induced downdrag is about 45.6 kips per 16-in pile (perimeter 4.19 ft × 18 ft × 0.55 × 1,100 psf). The static pile calculation CB-GEO-004 gives Qall = 240 kips (Qult 480/2), a 60-kip margin over the 180-kip service load. The as-built PDA end-of-drive CAPWAP values are 418–432 kips; at FS 2.0 the corresponding allowable is 209–216 kips, a margin of only 29–36 kips. The dewatering downdrag alone therefore consumes the PDA-based margin, giving utilisation (180 + 45.6)/209 to (180 + 45.6)/216 = 1.04 to 1.08. At the pile design's su of 1,820 psf, the same calculation gives about 75 kips of downdrag, which is worse. Calculation CB-GEO-004 (Item 049) did not include this drawdown case; the EOR must resolve the pile capacity and downdrag basis before any dewatering.
•  Mat edge, lateral support and heave. The 24-ft excavation removes about (12 × 133.2 + 12 × 120) × 2,992 sf ≈ 9,090 kips of overburden over the 68 × 44 ft pit. The resulting heave/rebound and lateral relief at the adjacent mat edge and piles are not checked; the shoring design treats the pit as a free perimeter. The mat is pile-supported, but its edge at the plant-room boundary loses lateral support and the clay beneath it will move.
•  Waterproofing and the K-5 joint. K-5 at grid K/5 is at the plant-room boundary (S-102 Rev.2; A-501 Rev.3). It uses Detail 1 positive-side bentonite membrane with a hydrophilic waterstop, rated to 20 ft head. The plant-room excavation is on the positive side; the membrane and waterstop may be exposed, damaged or reversed. The AOR/EOR must provide a plant-room boundary waterproofing detail and an inspection hold point. The C-4 leak (2–3 gpm on 07/01/2026, Zone 1) shows the basement envelope is not fully dry; dewatering will change the flow regime and may affect C-4/K-6. Coordinate with Item 056.
•  Permanent plant-room slab. Rev.2 says pumping continues until the plant-room slab is cast, but it does not check the slab for the full confined head El. 738.0 after pumping stops. The EOR must confirm the permanent slab and wall design and the transition from temporary dewatering. The drawdown also reduces hydrostatic uplift on the existing mat (a beneficial effect for the Item 050 buoyancy check), but that does not offset the settlement and downdrag and does not release the excavation.
•  Vibration. Sheet-pile driving and tieback drilling will occur within and adjacent to the completed mat and 48 piles. No vibration limit or monitoring is in the record. Require a pre-construction condition survey and vibration monitoring, with limits set by the EOR.

8 1.  PURPOSE
9 This memorandum records Thelbridge's verification of Item 048 on the Package A Review Comment and Verification Register. Item 048 is the delegated design of the temporary support of excavation (SOE) for the Block B plant-room excavation: Kesterline Submittal 31-SH-B Rev.1, sealed 06/11/2026, as supplemented by Revision 2 under letter KE-L-2026-0713, dated and sealed 07/13/2026. The excavation is 24 ft deep, from working grade El. 750.0 to plant-room subgrade El. 726.0, and is scheduled to start on 08/10/2026.
10 The determination is NOT VERIFIED. The current revision cannot be relied on for the excavation. Item 048 remains Open and the 08/10/2026 start is not released. The design's groundwater and stratigraphic values are correct, but its engineered-fill unit weight and undrained shear strength are not supported by the record; the toe-embedment, anchor-bond, sheet-pile flexure and wall-deflection checks fail on record inputs; the base-heave check passes only at the controlled head and fails at the design's own 727.0 ft stop-work trigger or with 0.5 ft of overdig; and the separately sealed Block B dewatering plan and the interface with the completed Block B mat, piles and K-5 joint are missing. Section 5 sets out what must be produced, by whom, and what this means for 08/10/2026.
12 2.  DOCUMENTS REVIEWED
13 The review was made against the following record. Revisions and dates are as stated in the documents. Where a document has been superseded in whole or in part, the governing part is identified.
14 Documents reviewed but not relied on: Rev.1 Section 2 and Section 3.4 dry-excavation assumption (Section 3.4 is superseded by Rev.2 R2.1; Section 2 remains in force but is contradicted by R2.1); 31-DW-A Block A well-point details (outside Block B); Calculation CB-GEO-004 (pile design, Item 049) and CB-STR-011 (mat design, Item 050), used only for interface checks; Sheet S-310/CB-STR-018 (podium, Item 055). The Rev.2 supplement is not entered in the Submittal Register; 31-SH-B Rev.1 is recorded as "Under review" as of 07/13/2026. All documents cited in Table 2-1 are the current revisions in the project record: GIR Rev.2 supersedes GIR Rev.1; DBM Rev.2 supersedes DBM Rev.1; Spec 31 20 00 Rev.3 supersedes Rev.2; S-101/S-201 Rev.4 supersede prior issues; A-501 Rev.3 supersedes prior revisions. Rev.1 of 31-SH-B is used only for the sections Rev.2 leaves in force, as identified in Finding 1.
16 3.  BASIS OF REVIEW
17 Precedence. DBM §1 states that the DBM governs all Package A calculations and controls subordinate documents; DBM §9 states that the GIR remains controlling for all soil parameters and any conflict is resolved in favour of the GIR. The GIR Rev.2 is therefore the governing source for groundwater, stratigraphy and soil strength. Rev.2's supersession matrix is applied only to the sections it expressly supersedes; sections left in force are checked for consistency with the new loads and geometry. RFI 104 and A-501 Rev.3 govern the permitted wall-to-mat joints; Spec 31 20 00 Articles 3.4.B and 3.6 govern fill acceptance and settlement; 31-DW-A Articles 1.2 and 4.2 govern the scope of dewatering. Where a requirement can be read two ways, the stricter reading is applied: the GIR upper-bound su of 1,100 psf, the record fill density, and a controlled head of 726.5 ft rather than the 727.0 ft trigger.
18 Table 3-1 — Governing parameters applied
19 Table 3-2 — Acceptance criteria applied
20 Method. The reviewer independently recomputed the active pressure (layered effective stress with hydrostatic water), passive resistance (total stress, su), free-earth toe moment, anchor force and bond, sheet-pile bending, wall deflection, base heave and dewatering consolidation. The designer's arithmetic was reproduced where the inputs are the same; differences are identified. The record fill unit weight is derived from the accepted fill: 95% of the Proctor maximum dry density 128.4 pcf, at the 9.2% optimum moisture, gives γtotal = 0.95 × 128.4 × 1.092 = 133.2 pcf (132.0 to 135.6 pcf over the permitted moisture window). The GIR su range of 900 to 1,100 psf is used; 1,100 psf is the upper bound and therefore the least conservative record value. The design's 1,400 psf is not supported by the GIR or the index data.
22 4.  FINDINGS
23 Finding 1 — Current revision and document status
24 Rev.2 is sealed and signed by B. A. Halvard, PE (Ohio P.E. No. E-58730, expires 12/31/2027) on 07/13/2026, so it is a valid later revision to the extent it supersedes Rev.1. However, the supersession matrix leaves Rev.1 Sections 1, 2, 3.1–3.3, 4.1, 4.2, 8, 11.3, 11.4, 12 and 13 in force. Four of those are inconsistent with Rev.2: (a) Section 2 still records the dry-excavation assumption of 31-DW-A, which Rev.2 Section 1 withdraws; (b) Section 11.3 still specifies a 28-ft PZ-35 single mill length, while Rev.2 R2.4 uses 30.5-ft sheets to tip El. 719.5; (c) Section 8's overturning and sliding checks use the Rev.1 loads (17,844 lb/ft) and toe El. 722.0, not the Rev.2 loads (19,610 lb/ft) and toe El. 719.5; (d) Section 13.1 item 2 still starts the Block A dewatering system (31-DW-A) 14 days before excavation, whereas Rev.2 relies on the Block B relief wells. In addition, the Rev.2 supplement is not logged in the Submittal Register (31-SH-B Rev.1 remains "Under review" as of 07/13/2026), and the Rev.1 Section 13 shoring drawings are not in the review file. The package is therefore not a complete, internally consistent design even before the numerical checks.
25 Finding 2 — Groundwater and stratigraphy are correctly stated
26 The GIR, the 19-round boring-log/monitoring record through 06/28/2026 and the Field Observation Report confirm the design water table El. 742.0 (range El. 741.6–742.4), the confined head El. 738.0 (range El. 737.7–738.3), the top of the confined aquifer El. 720.0, and the clay aquitard El. 738.0–720.0 (18 ft, 120 pcf). Borings B-04 and B-06 are inside the plant-room footprint and confirm the clay top and base. There is no evidence of a higher water table or a perched surface that would change the design groundwater. The groundwater values in Rev.2 are therefore verified and can be carried forward. What is not verified is the design's response: Rev.2 introduces active depressurization to El. 726.5 (11.5 ft of drawdown), whereas 31-DW-A Rev.1 and register Item 006 record a Block B cutoff wall toed at El. 722.0 with no active drawdown. That is a change of strategy, not a groundwater reading.
27 Finding 3 — The engineered-fill unit weight is understated (118 pcf vs 133.2 pcf)
28 Rev.2 uses 118 pcf for the 12 ft of engineered fill from El. 750.0 to El. 738.0 (R2.3). That is the GIR design unit weight for the upper sand, not for the compacted structural fill. The fill record RB-FPR-BB-2025 records 14 lifts, 12 ft, at 95% of the Proctor maximum 128.4 pcf and 9.2% optimum moisture. The corresponding total unit weight is 0.95 × 128.4 × 1.092 = 133.2 pcf (132.0–135.6 pcf over the permitted moisture window). Using 118 pcf understates the retained fill weight by about 11%.
29 Table 4-1 — Active lateral load, Rev.2 inputs vs record fill
30 The reviewer's layered integration reproduces the R2.3 load of 19,610 lb/ft but gives a driving moment of 227,532 ft-lb/ft, 4.1% below the 237,293 ft-lb/ft stated in R2.3; the designer's moment arm is conservative. The record fill increases the total horizontal load by 6.1% and reduces pn by 7.3% even at su 1,400 psf; the driver is the 5.9% increase in σv. The significant effect of the fill unit weight is on the passive resistance: even retaining the designer's su of 1,400 psf, the toe factor of safety falls from 1.62 (reviewer's reproduction) or 1.55 (Rev.2) to 1.43, below the required 1.50. The fill unit weight alone therefore fails the toe check; it also understates the anchor demand, flexure and deflection.
31 Finding 4 — The undrained shear strength is not supported by the GIR (1,400 psf vs 900–1,100 psf)
32 Rev.1 §3.2 and Rev.2 R2.4 use su = 1,400 psf. GIR §6.3 reports su = 900–1,100 psf from field vane and unconsolidated-undrained triaxial testing; the index and consolidation data contain no 1,400 psf value. DBM §9 makes the GIR controlling for soil parameters. A 1,400 psf value would require site-specific testing and a sealed geotechnical confirmation, neither of which is in the record. The reviewer notes that Calculation CB-GEO-004 uses an average su of 1,820 psf for pile shaft adhesion; that value is also outside the GIR range and is a separate inconsistency to be resolved under Item 049, but it cannot support the shoring value. Applying the upper bound of the logged range (1,100 psf) is the least conservative record-based value.
33 With record fill and su 1,100 psf: pn = 4(1,100) − 3,288 = 1,112 psf (vs 2,494 psf design); Pp = 1,112 × 6.5 = 7,225 lb/ft (vs 16,211); MR = 7,225 × 22.75 = 164,374 ft-lb/ft (vs 368,800); toe FS = 164,374 / 239,786 = 0.69. At su 900 psf, FS = 0.19. The required embedment at record inputs is about 12.6 ft (tip about El. 713.4) if clay passive is used over the full depth; the design provides 6.5 ft. The 1,400 psf value is the single largest non-conservative input in the design.
34 Finding 5 — Toe embedment fails on record inputs
35 Table 4-2 — Toe embedment factor of safety (criterion FS ≥ 1.50; D = 6.5 ft, tip El. 719.5)
36 Only the designer's 118 pcf / 1,400 psf case passes. Neither input is supported by the record. The toe check cannot be carried forward. A revised design must either increase the embedment (about 12.6 ft at record inputs, tip about El. 713.4, which penetrates the aquifer), add a second anchor level, or otherwise reduce the load. The current tip El. 719.5 is 0.5 ft into the aquifer; the design states that the sheet is not a cutoff and relies on the relief wells, but GIR §9.6 requires every penetration of the clay to be sealed at the aquitard. No interlock seal detail is in the record, and no seepage or piping check at the toe or along the sheet-soil interface is included. The 30.5-ft sheet also conflicts with Rev.1 §11.3's 28-ft sheet (Finding 1).
37 Finding 6 — The anchor bond zone is in clay, not dense sand and gravel; bond and proof test fail
38 The anchor is at El. 745.5, inclined 20° below horizontal, with 25 ft free length and 24 ft bond length (49 ft total). At 20° the anchor tip is at El. 745.5 − 49 sin 20° = El. 728.74. The bond zone runs from El. 736.95 to El. 728.74, entirely within the CL clay (El. 738.0–720.0). It does not reach the dense sand and gravel below El. 720.0; to do so would require (745.5 − 720.0)/sin 20° = 74.6 ft total. The 20 psi bond stress used in R2.5 is the FHWA-IF-99-015 Table 4 value for dense sand and gravel; it is not applicable to the clay actually penetrated. At the stiff-clay end of the same table (10 psi), the 24-ft bond gives Q = π × 0.5 × 24 × 10 × 144 = 54.3 kips, below the Rev.2 design load of 56.2 kips and far below the record design load of 102.0 kips.
39 Table 4-3 — Anchor demand, bond capacity and proof test (6 ft spacing, 20°; 24-ft bond, 6-in diameter)
40 Even if the bond were in sand, the record-fill / 1,100 psf demand gives FS 1.06 at 20 psi, below the 2.0 normally required for temporary ground anchors under FHWA-IF-99-015; the proof test of 135.7 kips exceeds the 108.6-kip bond capacity, so the anchor cannot be proof-tested to 1.33 × design. On the mat sides, the 49-ft anchors extend about 46 ft horizontally from the wall at El. 745.5, beneath the existing mat and across the 48-pile group; no clash or clearance check is in the record. RFI 048 only addresses 6-in clear to wall reinforcement. The anchor design cannot be carried forward.
41 Finding 7 — Sheet-pile flexure fails on record inputs
42 With Rev.2 inputs, Mmax = 62.4 kip-ft/ft at El. 733.1, Mallow = 121 kip-ft/ft and FS = 1.94; the reviewer reproduces 62.45 kip-ft/ft. 44 Finding 8 — Wall deflection exceeds H/200
45 Rev.2 predicts 1.3 in at El. 738.0 against H/200 = 1.44 in, a margin of only 0.14 in. The method is not independently reproducible from the record (no soil modulus or stiffness is stated), so the check is not verified; a revised deflection analysis is required. The deflection check cannot be carried forward.
46 Finding 9 — Base heave passes only at the controlled point; the operating envelope fails
47 The arithmetic is correct: W = 6.0 × 120 = 720 psf; 0.9W = 648 psf; at the controlled head El. 726.5, u = (726.5 − 720.0) × 62.4 = 405.6 psf; FS = 648 / 405.6 = 1.60, above 1.50. If the plug is 5.5 ft (0.5 ft of overdig), FS at 726.5 is 1.46 and at 727.0 is 1.36. At the initial head El. 738.0, FS is 0.58. The design has only a 6.7% margin at the controlled point, and its own trigger permits non-compliance. Pumping is the sole safeguard; there is no standby pump or power, automatic alarm, or response plan in the record.
48 Table 4-5 — Base-heave factor of safety vs head and plug thickness (criterion FS ≥ 1.50)
49 The base-heave formula can be carried forward only with the following conditions: stop-work trigger at or below El. 726.5 (preferably 726.0), no excavation below El. 726.0, continuous pumping with standby pumps and standby power, automatic high-head alarm, and a permanent plant-room slab designed for the full confined head El. 738.0. As written, the check is not verified.
50 Finding 10 — Global stability and overturning are stale and not updated for Rev.2
51 Rev.1 §8 remains in force under the Rev.2 matrix but was not updated. Its FS 2.06 uses the Rev.1 loads (17,844 lb/ft), passive 2,490 lb/ft and toe El. 722.0; none of these apply to Rev.2 (19,610 lb/ft, allowable passive 10,807 lb/ft, toe El. 719.5). That is an indicator that §8 was not updated, not a separate free-earth check; §8.2 treats the tieback reaction as an external resisting force, whereas R2.4 uses the free-earth formulation. The §8.1 "wall-free" sliding FS of 0.28 is not a design check with the tieback. The global stability section must be reissued. The design also does not check lateral support to the existing mat and piles, excavation unloading and heave, or vibration; those are addressed in Findings 11 and 12.

53 31-DW-A Rev.1 Article 1.2 expressly limits the plan to Block A and says the Block B plant-room will be addressed by a separate delegated design; Article 4.2 says the plan shall not be relied on for any design that assumes a reduction in the confined head below El. 738.0. SECTION 1 — DESIGN BASIS
1.1 General
These calculations establish the design of the temporary support of excavation for the deep plant-room excavation
planned beneath Block B of Package A of the Birchwood Village Expansion Program. The excavation is a
rectangular pit approximately 68 ft × 44 ft in plan, cut into the podium footprint east of the shared Block A/B
basement. Excavation commences from a working grade at El. 750.0 and terminates at a plant-room subgrade at
El. 726.0, a total excavated depth of 24 ft.
The temporary works described herein are the Contractor's means and methods and are supplied by delegated
1.2 Selected System
A driven steel sheet-pile wall, restrained by a single row of pre-stressed tieback anchors installed near the top of
the excavation, has been selected as the support system. The rationale is:
• (a) The excavation is deeper than would be economically supported by a cantilever wall;
• (b) A single-level tied wall provides adequate stiffness for the 24 ft depth without a soldier-pile / lagging
system, and drives to competent stratigraphy without an oversized toe;
• (c) A continuous sheet-pile section provides a substantially closed perimeter and does not rely on open-face
lagging.
Timber lagging with soldier piles was evaluated and rejected for this reason.

3.3 Design Approach — Blended Profile
For the calculation of the active pressure diagram behind the wall from working grade El. 750.0 down to
subgrade El. 726.0, a blended profile is adopted using a weighted average total unit weight of 119 pcf and an
equivalent effective friction angle of 30° (giving Ka = 0.333, Kp = 3.00). The blended profile provides a
conservative envelope that:
• (a) does not credit any cohesion contribution from the clay,
• (b) treats both strata as frictional with a single unified Ka, and
• (c) reproduces the vertical stress at subgrade within 1% of the layered calculation.
This is a standard simplification for the design of temporary sheet-pile walls of this proportion. The
blended-profile assumption is checked against a layered calculation in Section 5.3.
3.4 Groundwater Assumption for the Design Case
Per Section 2 above, and consistent with Reference R-3 (Contractor's dewatering plan, Submittal 31-DW-A), the
excavation is to be drawn down per Contractor's dewatering plan. Accordingly, the design case treated in
these calculations assumes dry conditions from working grade El. 750.0 down to subgrade El. 726.0 for the
duration of the temporary works. No pore water pressure is carried in the active or passive earth-pressure
diagrams below.

1.  EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
Kelbrook Geotechnical, Inc. has completed a subsurface investigation and geotechnical engineering analysis for
Package A of the Birchwood Village Expansion Program at 1802 Larchwood Avenue, Columbus, Ohio.
Package A comprises three student-housing blocks (Blocks A, B and C) constructed over a shared podium, with
a single basement level beneath Blocks A and B, and a separate deep plant-room excavation planned beneath
Block B.
The finished design grade across Package A is established at El. 750.0 ft. Existing ground surface stands at
approximately El. 750.0 across the footprints of Blocks A and C but falls to about El. 738.0 across the Block B
footprint (a former surface drainage swale). Placement of engineered fill of variable thickness — up to
approximately 12 ft beneath Block B — will therefore be required to bring the site to design grade.
The subsurface profile consists of three principal strata:
•  Stratum 1 — Upper sand, classified SP-SM (poorly-graded sand with silt), medium-dense, from
existing grade down to El. 738.0, total unit weight 118 pcf.
•  Stratum 2 — Compressible clay aquitard, classified CL (lean clay of medium plasticity),
normally-consolidated, from El. 738.0 down to El. 720.0 (18 ft thick), total unit weight 120 pcf, low
permeability. This is the strata governing settlement of shallow foundations and provides the aquitard
between the shallow and deep groundwater regimes.
•  Stratum 3 — Dense sand and gravel aquifer, classified SW-GW, below El. 720.0, total unit weight 130
pcf, confined by the overlying clay.
Groundwater is present as two distinct regimes:
•  The design water table in the upper sand is set at El. 742.0 ft. Piezometer readings taken from three
shallow standpipes over the 11/2024–02/2025 monitoring period range from El. 741.6 to El. 742.4;
groundwater seepage was observed at El. 741.8 to El. 742.2 in the Block A test-pit excavation.
•  A confined piezometric head of El. 738.0 ft has been measured in the deep sand-and-gravel aquifer
through two deep piezometers screened below El. 720.0, with readings ranging El. 737.7 to El. 738.3. The
confined head is at essentially the same elevation as the top of the clay aquitard.
Consolidation testing on two undisturbed Shelby-tube samples of the compressible clay (samples B-06 U3 and
B-08 U2, tested per ASTM D2435) yielded a compression index Cc = 0.28, a recompression index Cr = 0.045,
an initial void ratio e0 = 0.92, an in-situ vertical effective stress σ'0 = 1,850 psf, and a preconsolidation pressure
σ'p = 1,900 psf. The margin (σ'p − σ'0 ≈ 50 psf) confirms the clay is essentially normally-consolidated: any net
stress increase applied at the top of the clay will produce virgin (Cc) compression rather than recompression
(Cr) compression.
Principal geotechnical recommendations are as follows:
1.  Block C — Spread footings may be founded within the upper sand. Consolidation of the underlying
compressible clay under column-load stress increases at mid-depth of the clay must be explicitly computed
by the Structural Engineer of Record, using the parameters provided herein, and reconciled against the
settlement tolerances specified in the project structural criteria.
2.  Blocks A and B basement mat — A conventional reinforced-concrete mat foundation may be founded
within the upper sand at the design underside elevation. Hydrostatic uplift from the El. 742.0 water table
must be resolved by mat self-weight, superimposed permanent loads and, where necessary, tension
elements. The waterproofing system for the below-grade envelope must be selected for the applicable

2.3  Purpose and Scope of Investigation
The purpose of the investigation was to:
•  Characterize the subsurface soil profile, groundwater conditions and hydrogeologic regime across the
Package A footprint;
•  Recover and test representative undisturbed samples of the compressible clay stratum in order to develop
consolidation parameters for foundation-settlement analysis;
•  Provide geotechnical recommendations for the foundation of each block, for the design of the basement
mat and the plant-room excavation, and for the engineered fill required to bring the Block B footprint to
design grade; and
•  Provide construction considerations for dewatering, temporary excavation support and site preparation.
The scope of work comprised:
•  Nine (9) soil borings, B-01 through B-09, drilled to depths ranging 55 to 90 ft below existing ground
surface;
•  Installation of five (5) monitoring installations (three shallow standpipe piezometers screened in the
upper sand and two deep piezometers screened in the dense sand and gravel below El. 720.0);
•  Recovery of representative split-spoon (SPT) samples on 2.5 ft or 5 ft centers and thin-walled
(Shelby-tube) undisturbed samples of the CL clay at selected borings;
•  Laboratory classification, index and consolidation testing (ASTM D2435, ASTM D698, ASTM D1557);
•  Engineering analysis and preparation of this report.

3.  SITE DESCRIPTION AND GEOLOGIC SETTING
3.1  Site Location and Topography
The Package A site is located at 1802 Larchwood Avenue, on the western portion of the Thornbury State
University main campus in Columbus, Ohio. The site is bounded to the north by Larchwood Avenue, to the east
by an existing campus surface parking lot, to the south by an unimproved landscaped strip and to the west by an
existing academic building. The overall Package A footprint is approximately 3.7 acres.
Existing topography varies substantially across 
 Ground surface stands at approximately El. 750.0 ft
across the footprints of Blocks A and C in the northern and eastern portions of 
 Toward the southwest,
across the footprint of Block B, ground surface falls to about El. 738.0 ft (a difference of about 12 ft) in what
appears from historical aerial photography to have been a surface drainage swale draining the pre-development
ground westward toward a former off-site low area. The transition between the two elevations is gradual across
a nominal 60 to 80 ft width. Existing ground within Block B is generally covered with a thin (~0.5 to 1 ft)
mantle of soft organic-rich silty topsoil overlying the SP-SM upper sand; no fill of engineering significance is
present beneath Block B in its current condition.
3.2  Regional and Local Geology
Columbus, Ohio lies within the Till Plains section of the Central Lowland physiographic province. Regional
surficial geology is dominated by Wisconsinan-age glacial deposits — chiefly clay-rich till, glaciolacustrine silt
and clay, and outwash sand and gravel — overlying Devonian-age carbonate and shale bedrock. Local
hydrogeology is characterized by a shallow phreatic surface within the outwash and reworked outwash sands, a
laterally continuous fine-grained aquitard, and a lower confined aquifer within basal outwash sand and gravel
above bedrock.
The subsurface conditions encountered in the Package A borings are consistent with this regional framework: a
medium-dense reworked outwash sand at the surface, a low-permeability clay of glaciolacustrine origin at
intermediate depth, and a dense outwash sand and gravel aquifer at depth. Bedrock was not encountered within
the maximum boring depth of 90 ft (approximately El. 660.0). Blow counts in the SW-GW below El. 720.0
were consistently in the range N ≥ 50 blows per 6 inches, indicating a very dense sand-and-gravel deposit
suitable as a pile-bearing stratum.
3.3  Site History and Prior Use
Site historical review — including review of Franklin County parcel records, USGS topographic maps (1955
and later editions), and Thornbury State University campus master planning archives — indicates that the
Package A parcel was in agricultural use through approximately 1958, was acquired by the University in 1962,
and has been used for surface parking and landscape maintenance since. No prior structures of consequence, no
known below-grade utilities (other than a single abandoned 6-inch clay drain traced along the historic swale in
Block B), and no known industrial fill are present within the footprint. Because there is essentially no prior fill
of engineering significance, the Block B footprint requires new engineered fill — placed on the natural
clay-upper-sand contact after removal of the topsoil mantle — to bring the site to design grade.

PART 1    GENERAL
1.1   SUMMARY
A.   Section Includes:
1.   Excavation, subgrade preparation, and grading for building foundations, mat foundations,
pile caps, footings, and slabs-on-grade within the Package A limits of work.
2.   Placement, moisture-conditioning, and compaction of engineered structural fill under
building foundations and slabs-on-grade.
3.   Backfill against foundation walls and around subsurface structures.
4.   Field quality control by the Owner's independent testing laboratory.
B.   Related Sections:
1.   Section 31 23 33 — Trenching and Backfilling for utility trenches within the building
envelope.
2.   Section 31 50 00 — Excavation Support and Protection for delegated shoring design.
3.   Section 03 30 00 — Cast-in-Place Concrete for placement of concrete against completed
subgrade.
1.2   REFERENCES
A.   Referenced Standards. The following standards are incorporated by reference to the extent
cited herein. The latest edition in effect at the date of Contract award shall govern.
1.   ASTM D698 — Standard Test Methods for Laboratory Compaction Characteristics of
Soil Using Standard Effort (Standard Proctor). Cited for historical borrow characterization
only; not the acceptance basis for Package A structural fill.
2.   ASTM D1557 — Standard Test Methods for Laboratory Compaction Characteristics of
Soil Using Modified Effort (Modified Proctor). Governing laboratory reference for
Package A structural fill.
3.   ASTM D6938 — Standard Test Methods for In-Place Density and Water Content of Soil
and Soil-Aggregate by Nuclear Methods (Shallow Depth). Governing field density test
method.
4.   ASTM D2216 — Standard Test Methods for Laboratory Determination of Water
(Moisture) Content of Soil and Rock by Mass. Referee method for moisture content

--- page 2 ---
when the nuclear gauge reading is disputed.
5.   ASTM D2937 — Standard Test Method for Density of Soil in Place by the Drive-Cylinder
Method. Alternate field density method where permitted in writing by the Structural
Engineer of Record.
1.3   DEFINITIONS
A.   Structural Fill: Imported or on-site engineered soil placed and compacted in controlled lifts
beneath building foundations, mat foundations, pile caps, footings, or slabs-on-grade, and
meeting the material, gradation, and compaction requirements of this Section.
B.   Common Fill: Non-structural earth used only for site grading outside the building envelope.
C.   Lift: A single layer of loose fill placed in preparation for compaction, not exceeding the
maximum loose lift thickness specified in Part 3.
D.   Test Location: A single field-density test point at which both dry density and moisture
content are measured for compliance evaluation.
E.   Placed Material: The specific soil material actually placed in the field at the test location,
whose laboratory maximum dry density and optimum moisture content have been established
by ASTM D1557 Method C laboratory testing prior to placement, as required by Article 2.1.
1.4   QUALITY ASSURANCE
A.   Testing Laboratory. Field and laboratory testing under this Section shall be performed by the
Owner's independent construction materials testing laboratory (the “Laboratory”), contracted
directly to the Owner. The Contractor shall coordinate access, sampling opportunity, and
lift-by-lift notification with the Laboratory.
B.   Personnel. Nuclear-gauge operators shall hold current radiation safety training and shall be
documented as competent in ASTM D6938 direct-transmission procedures. Nuclear gauges
shall be calibrated within the manufacturer's stated interval and standard-count checked at
the start of each testing day.
C.   Placed-Material Correspondence. The laboratory maximum dry density and optimum
moisture content used as the acceptance denominators for any test location shall be those
determined by ASTM D1557 Method C on the material actually placed at that location. Where
the placed material differs materially from the previously characterized borrow, a new ASTM
D1557 Method C test shall be performed on the new material before further fill placement is
accepted.
1.5   SUBMITTALS
A.   Prior to structural fill placement, submit for review:
1.   Source identification for each proposed borrow, including gradation (sieve analysis),
Atterberg limits, and USCS classification.
2.   Laboratory report of maximum dry density and optimum moisture content per ASTM
D1557 Method C for each proposed source material.
3.   Placement and compaction plan identifying lift thickness, compaction equipment, and
passes.
B.   During placement, submit daily:
31 20 00 - Page 2 of 6
Earth Moving


--- page 3 ---
1.   Field density reports per ASTM D6938 identifying test location, lift number, elevation, dry
density, moisture content, the ASTM D1557 Method C laboratory maximum dry density
and optimum moisture content used as denominators, percent compaction, and moisture
deviation from optimum.
1.6   SEQUENCING
A.   No structural fill shall be placed until the underlying subgrade has been proof-rolled in the
presence of the Laboratory and accepted in writing by the Owner's Representative Engineer.
B.   No fill placement shall proceed on any lift until the preceding lift has been tested and
accepted per Article 3.4.
PART 2    PRODUCTS
2.1   STRUCTURAL FILL
A.   Material. Well-graded granular fill classified SM or SW-SM, laboratory-tested per ASTM
D1557 Method C (modified Proctor) prior to placement.
B.   Gradation. Structural fill shall meet the following gradation, with no more than 12% passing
the No. 200 sieve and a plasticity index not exceeding 6.
C.   Deleterious Material. Structural fill shall be free of organic material, frozen soil, debris, and
particles greater than 3 inches in largest dimension.
D.   Laboratory Characterization. For each source and for each material change, the Laboratory
shall determine the maximum dry density and optimum moisture content by ASTM D1557
Method C prior to placement. The resulting laboratory values are the denominators against
which the acceptance criteria of Article 3.4.B are evaluated.
2.2   COMMON FILL
A.   Common fill placed outside the building envelope shall be free of organic material, debris, and
frozen soil, but is not subject to the acceptance criteria of Article 3.4.B.
2.3   CAPILLARY BREAK / DRAINAGE COURSE
A.   Clean, open-graded crushed stone, 3/4 in nominal, less than 2% passing the No. 200 sieve,
placed as shown on the Drawings beneath slabs-on-grade.
PART 3    EXECUTION
3.1   EXAMINATION
A.   Examine subgrade prior to fill placement. Do not proceed with fill placement over subgrade
that is soft, yielding under proof roll, frozen, or otherwise unsuitable. Notify the Owner's
Representative Engineer in writing of any unsuitable subgrade condition.
3.2   SUBGRADE PREPARATION
A.   Strip topsoil, organic material, and any existing uncontrolled fill from beneath the footprint of
structural fill.
B.   Proof-roll exposed subgrade with a loaded tandem-axle dump truck or equivalent equipment
approved in writing by the Owner's Representative Engineer. The Laboratory shall be present
31 20 00 - Page 3 of 6
Earth Moving


--- page 4 ---
to witness the proof roll.
C.   Undercut and replace yielding areas with structural fill placed and compacted per this
Section.
3.3   PLACEMENT
A.   Place structural fill in horizontal lifts not exceeding 12 inches loose thickness.
B.   Moisture-condition each lift, by wetting or drying and mixing, so that the moisture content at
the time of compaction is within the range specified in Article 3.4.B.
C.   Compact each lift with equipment sized and operated to achieve the density and moisture
requirements of Article 3.4.B throughout the full thickness of the lift.
D.   Do not place fill on frozen subgrade or with frozen material. Do not place fill during
precipitation that raises the placed material's moisture content above the upper limit of Article
3.4.B.
3.4   COMPACTION
A.   Method Statement. The Contractor shall place structural fill in controlled lifts as specified in
Article 3.3, moisture-conditioning each lift as necessary to bring the material within the
moisture range required by Article 3.4.B before compaction. Compaction equipment
(self-propelled vibratory smooth-drum rollers, pad-foot rollers, or plate compactors adjacent to
structures) shall be operated in a pattern of overlapping passes such that every location
within a lift receives no fewer than the number of passes established during a
Contractor-conducted test strip witnessed by the Laboratory and the Owner's Representative
Engineer. The test strip shall be executed at the start of production placement, using the
placement source, moisture-conditioning method, lift thickness, and compaction equipment
intended for production, and shall demonstrate that the criteria of Article 3.4.B are met before
general production is authorized. Adjacent to walls, columns, and utilities, use hand-operated
compaction equipment in lifts not exceeding 6 inches loose thickness. Do not operate heavy
compaction equipment within 3 feet of walls prior to backfill balancing on both sides. Each lift
shall be tested and accepted per Article 3.4.B before the next lift is placed.
B.   Acceptance Criteria.
Structural fill shall be placed and compacted to a dry density of not less than
95% of the maximum dry density determined by ASTM D1557 Method C for the
placed material, AND shall be placed at a moisture content within −1% to +2%
of the optimum moisture content determined by the same test. Both criteria must
be satisfied for each test location. Field density shall be measured per ASTM
D6938 (nuclear gauge, direct-transmission mode) at a frequency of one test per
5,000 sf per lift.
C.   Failing Tests. Where either the density criterion or the moisture criterion of Article 3.4.B is
not satisfied at any test location:
1.   The affected area of the lift shall be reworked (scarified, moisture-conditioned, and
recompacted, or removed and replaced) at the Contractor's expense.
2.   Reworked areas shall be retested by the Laboratory. Both the density and moisture
criteria of Article 3.4.B must be satisfied on the retest before the lift is accepted.

compliance. Acceptance is evaluated at each test location independently.
D.   Interpretation. No test location shall be accepted on the basis of density alone. No test
location shall be accepted on the basis of moisture alone. Compliance requires that both the
density criterion and the moisture criterion of Article 3.4.B be independently satisfied at that
test location, as measured against the ASTM D1557 Method C laboratory maximum dry
density and optimum moisture content of the material actually placed at that location.
3.5   BACKFILL AGAINST FOUNDATION WALLS
A.   Do not commence backfill against basement or foundation walls until the wall has attained its
specified 28-day compressive strength, or until permanent lateral support (floor framing) is in
place and grouted to the wall, whichever occurs first.
B.   Place backfill on both sides of interior walls in balanced lifts not exceeding 12 inches loose
thickness, differing by no more than one lift side-to-side.
C.   Compact backfill to the same acceptance criteria as Article 3.4.B where the backfill supports
structure or slabs; elsewhere, to 90% of ASTM D1557 Method C maximum dry density.
3.6   SETTLEMENT TOLERANCE
A.   Total and Differential Settlement. Total settlement 1.0 in maximum; differential settlement
0.5 in maximum over 30 ft.
B.   Application. The tolerances of Paragraph A apply to the completed foundation system as
constructed on the accepted subgrade and structural fill delivered under this Section. Where
predicted or monitored settlements exceed the tolerances of Paragraph A, the Structural
Engineer of Record shall be notified in writing and no additional load shall be applied until a
written disposition is issued.
C.   Monitoring. Where settlement monitoring points are shown on the Drawings, readings shall
be taken and transmitted to the Owner's Representative Engineer at the frequency indicated.
Cumulative settlement approaching either tolerance of Paragraph A shall be reported
immediately.
3.7   FIELD QUALITY CONTROL
A.   Testing frequency for structural fill:
1.   In-place density and moisture: one ASTM D6938 test per 5,000 sf per lift, as required by
Article 3.4.B, and not fewer than three tests per lift regardless of lift area.
2.   Laboratory maximum dry density and optimum moisture content: one ASTM D1557
Method C determination per source, and one additional determination for each material
change identified by visual classification or gradation.
B.   Reporting. The Laboratory shall issue field density reports within 24 hours of testing. Each
report shall identify, for each test location, the ASTM D1557 Method C laboratory maximum
dry density and optimum moisture content used as the denominators, the measured dry
density, the measured moisture content, the percent compaction, the moisture deviation from
optimum, and the disposition (accept or reject) against Article 3.4.B.
C.   Non-Conforming Work. Any lift not meeting Article 3.4.B, or any lift for which the ASTM
D1557 Method C denominators used in reporting do not correspond to the material actually
placed, shall be reworked as required by Article 3.4.C before any additional lift is placed.

PART 1 — SCOPE
1.1 General
This document constitutes the dewatering and groundwater control plan required under Specification Section 31
23 19 for construction of the Block A basement excavation on Package A of the Birchwood Village Expansion
Program. It defines the design assumptions, method of dewatering, discharge arrangement, monitoring provisions
and limitations of the temporary works.
1.2 Scope of Work — Explicit
This dewatering plan addresses dewatering of the Block A basement excavation only, to subgrade El. 730.0
approximate. It does NOT extend to the separate deep excavation planned beneath Block B, which will be
addressed by a separate delegated design.
For the avoidance of doubt: no interior drawdown system is proposed for Block B under this plan; groundwater
within the Block B enclosure will be managed by sump control of surface and construction water only. The Block
B plant-room excavation is enclosed by a separate slurry cutoff wall keyed a minimum of 4 ft into the
compressible clay stratum (toe at El. 722.0), covered under a separate submittal.
The following are expressly outside the scope of this submittal:
(a) Any excavation, cofferdam, cutoff wall or shoring system beneath, adjacent to, or in support of construction
other than the Block A basement excavation defined above;
(b) Any dewatering operation targeted at, or intended to relieve pressure in, the confined aquifer underlying the
site (see Part 4 — Limitations);
(c) Any groundwater control associated with the deeper subsurface work planned under Block B, which is being
carried under a separate submittal package by others.
Any subsequent excavation extending below approximate El. 730.0, or approaching the confined aquifer beneath
the compressible clay aquitard, will require a separately-sealed dewatering and groundwater control analysis.
Nothing in this submittal shall be relied upon to demonstrate stability of, or groundwater control for, work outside
the Block A basement footprint defined in Article 1.1.
1.3 Reference Documents
• Geotechnical Investigation Report, Birchwood Village Package A, Kelbrook Geotechnical, Inc., Report No.
KGI-2024-0417, Rev.2, 02/14/2025. (Referenced herein as "the Geotechnical Report.")

Groundwater conditions applicable to the Block A basement excavation are as described in Section 7 of the
Geotechnical Report and are summarized below.
Design water table (upper sand): El. 742.0 ft. Shallow standpipe monitoring across the site from 11/22/2024

vertical hydraulic communication is developed across it.

PART 3 — METHOD OF DEWATERING
3.1 Selected Method
Dewatering of the Block A basement excavation shall be accomplished by a single-stage perimeter well-point
system installed in the upper sand around the Block A basement footprint. Well points shall draw the upper
phreatic surface down from El. 742.0 to a working elevation of El. 728.0 (approximately 2 ft below the design
subgrade of El. 730.0) for the duration of below-grade construction within Block A.
The well-point system is intended solely to relieve the shallow phreatic surface in the upper sand within the Block
A footprint. It is not designed to, and does not, address the confined piezometric head in the deep aquifer (see Part
4).
3.2 Well-Point Layout
Twenty-four (24) well points shall be installed around the perimeter of the Block A basement excavation,
arranged approximately as follows:

Well-point details:
• Riser: 2-inch nominal Schedule 40 PVC, jetted-in.
• Screen: 2-inch nominal PVC screen, slot 0.020 in, 5 ft length, seated between approximately El. 738.5 and El.
733.5.
• Filter pack: uniform silica sand, 20/40, placed to at least 1 ft above screen.
• Header main: 6-inch nominal HDPE header, welded joints, laid at approximately El. 745, connected to well
points via flexible swing-arm risers.
• Pumps: two (2) Thompson 6 in diesel wellpoint pumps, one duty and one standby, sized for the combined
discharge with 25% reserve capacity; automatic transfer on primary loss of vacuum or flow.
• Vacuum: system designed for steady-state vacuum of 20 to 25 in Hg at the header main.
Each well-point riser shall be capped with a shut-off valve at the header connection to allow individual isolation
for maintenance without shutdown of the surrounding system.
3.3 Startup and Steady-State Operation


--- page 6 ---

Startup shall commence not less than fourteen (14) calendar days prior to the beginning of below-grade
excavation within Block A. Excavation shall not proceed until:
(a) The observed drawdown at the interior of the Block A footprint has stabilized at or below El. 728.0 for not
less than seventy-two (72) continuous hours, and
(b) All three shallow observation piezometers (see Article 3.5) have produced readings within 0.3 ft of the
target drawdown for two consecutive twice-daily reads.
Steady-state pumping shall continue continuously (24 hours per day, 7 days per week) from startup through
completion of the basement mat, exterior basement wall waterproofing, and backfill of the exterior wall to a level
adequate to resist buoyancy of the mat under design head. Shutdown shall be executed by the Contractor only
with written concurrence of the Owner's Representative.
3.4 Discharge
Discharge from the well-point pumps shall be routed to the campus storm sewer system, in accordance with the
discharge permit obtained by the Contractor from the City of Columbus. Discharge routing is as follows:
• Header main discharge → in-line flow meter and sediment trap → 8-inch HDPE lay-flat conveyance line →
sediment control basin at Grid J-7 (approx. 40 ft × 20 ft × 4 ft deep, lined) → outfall pipe to existing storm
manhole SM-14 at the northwest corner of the site.
Design steady-state discharge is estimated at 55 gpm from the combined system (based on Sichardt-type radius of
influence calculations for the upper sand with representative permeability of 5 × 10-3 cm/s). The discharge permit
obtained by the Contractor is issued for peak flows up to 100 gpm.
Water quality at the discharge point shall be checked twice weekly for turbidity and pH; results shall be recorded
in the dewatering log required under Article 3.6.
3.5 Monitoring — Shallow Piezometers
Drawdown of the upper phreatic surface shall be monitored by three (3) shallow standpipe observation
piezometers, installed within the Block A footprint prior to startup. Piezometer locations shall be selected to
represent the interior response of the excavation:
• OP-1: approximate center of Block A footprint.
• OP-2: midway between the west perimeter well-point line and the geometric center.
• OP-3: midway between the north perimeter well-point line and the geometric center.
Each observation piezometer shall be a 2-inch PVC standpipe with a 5-ft screen set between approximately El.
738 and El. 733, sanded around the screen and grouted above. Water levels shall be read twice daily during
startup, once daily during steady-state operation, and hourly during any period when a duty pump is out of
service.
Readings shall be recorded in a dewatering log maintained by the Contractor's superintendent and made available
to the Owner's Representative on request. The log shall record: date and time; pump status (duty/standby);
observed water level at OP-1, OP-2, OP-3; system vacuum; header main discharge flow; discharge turbidity and
pH (twice weekly); and any operational events (pump changeover, header repair, weather).
3.6 Contingency
Loss of drawdown at any of the three observation piezometers by more than 1.0 ft from the target El. 728.0,
sustained for more than four (4) hours during active excavation or four (4) hours during any 24-hour period of
steady-state operation, shall constitute a system exception. On any such exception the Contractor shall:
(a) Immediately transfer to the standby pump and diagnose the duty pump;


--- page 7 ---

Page 7
(b) Notify the Owner's Representative and the Structural Engineer of Record in writing within four (4) hours;
and
(c) Suspend any excavation activity within Block A until the drawdown target is re-established.
PART 4 — LIMITATIONS
4.1 Confined Aquifer
Because the confined aquifer at El. 720.0 is separated from the upper sand by the CL aquitard El. 738.0 to El.
720.0, dewatering by perimeter well points in the upper sand will not reduce the confined head. The confined
piezometric head at El. 738.0 is developed in the deep sand and gravel below El. 720.0 and is sustained by a
source of recharge that is hydraulically decoupled from the shallow phreatic surface targeted by this system.
Any excavation extending toward or into the confined aquifer will require separate analysis. Such analysis shall
address, at minimum: (a) the residual thickness of the clay aquitard beneath the excavation subgrade; (b) the
weight of that residual plug relative to the confined uplift acting on its underside at El. 720.0; (c) the factor of
safety against base heave; and (d) whether relief of the confined head, by means outside the scope of this
submittal (e.g., deep relief wells screened in the sand and gravel), is required to establish an adequate factor of
safety.
Nothing in this submittal has been designed to, and nothing in this submittal shall be construed to, relieve the
confined piezometric head.
4.2 Adjacent and Subsequent Work
This plan is limited to the Block A basement excavation defined in Article 1.2. It shall not be relied upon by
others as the basis for:
(a) Design of temporary shoring outside the Block A footprint;
(b) Design of excavation support, cofferdams or cutoff walls beneath Block B or elsewhere on the site;
(c) Any calculation that treats the excavation as dry, dewatered or relieved outside the extents shown in Article
3.2 above;
(d) Any design that assumes a reduction in the confined piezometric head below El. 738.0 at any location.
Any delegated design outside the Block A basement footprint shall independently verify the groundwater
conditions applicable to that work directly from the Geotechnical Report or from a separately-sealed
hydrogeologic evaluation. The undersigned engineer's seal below applies only to the temporary works described
in this submittal, within the scope defined in Article 1.2, and only for the Block A basement excavation.
4.3 Duration
This plan is prepared for the temporary construction duration of the Block A below-grade work. It does not
constitute a permanent groundwater control system and does not address long-term dewatering. Permanent
below-grade water management for the completed structure is addressed under separate design by the Architect
of Record and Structural Engineer of Record (below-grade waterproofing and drainage details, see Package A
architectural and structural documents).
4.4 Weather and Recharge
The upper sand phreatic surface in the vicinity of the excavation may respond to seasonal recharge from
significant precipitation events. The 25% reserve pump capacity provided under Article 3.2 is intended to
accommodate ordinary seasonal fluctuation. Extraordinary precipitation events (e.g., a 10-year 24-hour event)
may require additional temporary measures to be added by the Contractor.

horizontal blindside, vertical wall and wall-to-mat construction joint conditions where hydrostatic pressure is present.

1. PURPOSE AND SCOPE
This memorandum establishes the governing codes, reference standards, site parameters, design loads, load
combinations, and serviceability criteria adopted for the structural design of Package A of the Birchwood Village
Expansion. Package A comprises three student-housing blocks (Blocks A, B and C) constructed over a shared
podium, one basement level beneath Blocks A and B, and a separate deep plant-room excavation planned beneath
Block B. The design basis stated herein governs all Package A calculations, drawings, and specifications issued
by the Engineer of Record and controls the interpretation of subordinate design documents where a conflict
arises.

Revision Block on the final page.

• Ohio Building Code (2024 edition, adopting IBC 2021 with Ohio amendments) — governing building
code as adopted by the State of Ohio; Chapter 16 (Structural Design) references ASCE 7-16 for loads.

design, detailing, cover, and serviceability.
• ASCE 7-16, Minimum Design Loads and Associated Criteria for Buildings and Other Structures — dead,
live, snow, wind, seismic loads and load combinations.
• AISC 360-16, Specification for Structural Steel Buildings — structural steel members and connections at
podium framing and roof.
• ACI 301-20 for cast-in-place concrete construction requirements referenced through Spec 03 30 00.
• ASCE 32-01 for frost-protected shallow foundations where applicable at Block C perimeter.

(Rev.2, current at the date of this memorandum), and where cited by ASTM designation on the drawings.

import numpy as np
q=250;g1=118;g2=120;Ka1=.307;Ka2=.390
z=np.linspace(0,24,240001);dz=z[1]-z[0]
sv=np.where(z<=12,q+g1*z,q+g1*12+g2*(z-12));Ka=np.where(z<=12,Ka1,Ka2)
p=Ka*sv
print('total stress no water P',np.sum(p)*dz,'M',np.sum(p*(4.5-z))*dz)
# effective stress with water and p=Ka*sv_eff only (no water lateral)
u=np.where(z>8,(z-8)*62.4,0); pe=Ka*(sv-u)
print('eff soil only P',np.sum(pe)*dz,'M',np.sum(pe*(4.5-z))*dz)
# blended Ka .333, total stress
print('blended total P',np.sum(.333*sv)*dz,'M',np.sum(.333*sv*(4.5-z))*dz)
# blended eff
print('blended eff P',np.sum(.333*(sv-u))*dz,'M',np.sum(.333*(sv-u)*(4.5-z))*dz)
EOF

1. Purpose and Scope
This field observation report documents excavation observations, groundwater monitoring readings and seepage
observations recorded by Kelbrook Geotechnical field personnel across the Package A footprint over the
construction period 07/2025 through 05/2026. The observations reported herein are drawn from the writer’s
daily field notes, from the shallow standpipe and deep piezometer monitoring log maintained under the ongoing
Package A groundwater monitoring program, and from photographs and sketches taken at the time of
observation. The report is furnished in support of the Owner’s Representative construction verification file and
as supplemental record to the Geotechnical Investigation Report Rev.2 (KGI-2024-0417).
Two distinct field episodes are documented: (a) the Block A basement excavation, opened in the summer of
2025 to a working subgrade at approximately El. 730.0; and (b) the placement of engineered fill across the
Block B footprint from 10/06/2025 through 11/02/2025 and the subsequent months of pile installation and
lift-up to design grade. Groundwater monitoring is continuous across both episodes and is reported in full.
2. Excavation Observations — Block A Basement
2.1 Excavation Opening and Progression
Adrian Vance


--- page 2 ---
Kelbrook Geotechnical, Inc.
Report No. KGI-FO-2026-0528
Field Observation Report — Excavation and Groundwater — Package A
Page 2
The Block A basement excavation was opened in the northeast quadrant of the Package A footprint on
07/14/2025 and progressed from existing grade El. 750.0 down to a working subgrade at approximately El.
730.0 (approximately one foot below the design underside of the basement mat at El. 731.5, to accommodate a
lean-concrete working mat). The excavation was carried out by the Contractor using a mid-size hydraulic
excavator with side dumping to trucks; sequence proceeded from the east perimeter westward across the Block
A footprint over the course of approximately three weeks.
Perimeter shoring — a combination of soldier pile and timber lagging along the northern and eastern faces, and
open-cut battered slopes along the interior (Block A / Block B transition) — was installed ahead of the cut face.
Well-point dewatering, executed per the Contractor’s Dewatering and Groundwater Control Plan Rev.1
dated 06/04/2025, was activated on 07/12/2025, two days before the first cut, and remained in operation
continuously through mat placement on 01/12/2026 and thereafter to protect the wall pour sequence.
2.2 Side Conditions Observed in the Cut Face
Exposed cut faces along the Block A perimeter revealed the following, consistent with the strata described in
Section 6 of the reference report:
•
From existing grade El. 750.0 down to approximately El. 746.0: approximately 4 ft of loose topsoil,
root-mat and reworked surface fill of engineering significance limited to the upper 0.5 to 1 ft, transitioning
downward into weathered upper sand. This layer was over-excavated and hauled off-site as unsuitable for
structural fill re-use.
•
From approximately El. 746.0 down to El. 738.0: the SP-SM upper sand — medium-dense, moist above
the water table and saturated below it, with a modest silt content and no interbedded fine-grained seams.
Cut face stability in the sand above the water table was satisfactory at 1H:1V; below the water table (once
dewatered) the face was cut vertically against the shoring without slumping.
•
From El. 738.0 down to the working subgrade at El. 730.0: the top of the CL clay aquitard, exposed as
a stiff, medium-plasticity lean clay of grey-brown colour. The top of the clay at El. 738.0 was consistent
within ± 0.5 ft across the Block A footprint. The clay retained a vertical or near-vertical face for the
excavation duration without noticeable creep or heave; subgrade compaction footprint (proof-rolling)
produced no rutting or pumping under the loaded haul truck used for the check.
The transition from Stratum 1 (upper sand) to Stratum 2 (clay) at El. 738.0 was sharp and well-defined in the cut
face and matched the elevation logged in Borings B-01, B-02, B-07 and B-09 within a few tenths of a foot.
2.3 Working Subgrade Condition
Subgrade at El. 730.0 was inspected on 08/06/2025 in the presence of the Contractor’s Superintendent (Mr.
Marcus Whitfield) and the Owner’s Representative (Mr. 
). Subgrade was found to be firm,
uniform, free of standing water within the dewatered footprint, and suitable to receive the lean-concrete
working mat and subsequently the reinforced mat foundation. No soft spots, disturbed zones or unsuitable
inclusions were logged. The subgrade approval memorandum was issued separately by Kelbrook on
08/07/2025.
3. Groundwater Monitoring — Continuous Record
Groundwater monitoring under the Package A program continues from the piezometer array installed
11/22/2024 and reported in the Geotechnical Investigation Report Rev.2. Over the observation period 07/2025
rounds since installation. Readings are taken monthly (weekly during active excavation and dewatering).
through 05/2026 an additional eleven monitoring rounds were completed, bringing the total record to eighteen
Adrian Vance


--- page 3 ---
Kelbrook Geotechnical, Inc.
Report No. KGI-FO-2026-0528
Field Observation Report — Excavation and Groundwater — Package A
Page 3
3.1 Design Water Table — Upper Sand (Shallow Standpipe Piezometers)
The design water table in the upper SP-SM sand, established at El. 742.0 in the reference report, is confirmed
by the extended monitoring record. Readings from the three shallow standpipe piezometers (B-01, B-03, B-09),
taken across the 07/2025 through 05/2026 observation period at locations outside the Block A dewatered
footprint, remain in the range El. 741.6 to El. 742.4, with individual monthly means clustered within a few
tenths of a foot of El. 742.0. No systematic trend, no seasonal excursion beyond that range and no departure
from the design elevation was recorded.
3.2 Confined Piezometric Head — Deep Aquifer (Deep Piezometers)
The confined piezometric head in the deep SW-GW sand-and-gravel aquifer below El. 720.0, established at El.
738.0 in the reference report, is likewise confirmed. Readings from the two deep piezometers (B-04 and B-08),
both screened below El. 720.0 within the Block B footprint, remain in the range El. 737.7 to El. 738.3 across
the full extended record. The head is stable, without trend, and consistent with the value carried forward from
the Rev.2 investigation.
