VERIFICATION MEMORANDUM

To:	Rachel Marlbeck, University Program Director, Thornbury State University

From:	Adrian Vance, Project Engineer (Structural/Geotechnical), Thelbridge Project Management Services, Owner's Representative

Date:	July 20, 2026

Subject:	Item 048 — Block B Plant-Room Shoring: Verification of Kesterline Submittal 31-SH-B Rev.1 (sealed 06/11/2026) as supplemented by Rev.2 (KE-L-2026-0713, sealed 07/13/2026) — NOT VERIFIED

cc:  Steven Kendrow, Rowan Bay Constructors, Inc.; Gregory Nash, PE, Calloway Braddock Structural Engineers, LLC; Rahul Nimkar, Thelbridge Project Management Services (Geotechnical Reviewer); Project File

1.  PURPOSE

This memorandum records Thelbridge's verification of Item 048 on the Package A Review Comment and Verification Register. Item 048 is the delegated design of the temporary support of excavation (SOE) for the Block B plant-room excavation: Kesterline Submittal 31-SH-B Rev.1, sealed 06/11/2026, as supplemented by Revision 2 under letter KE-L-2026-0713, dated and sealed 07/13/2026. The excavation is 24 ft deep, from working grade El. 750.0 to plant-room subgrade El. 726.0, and is scheduled to start on 08/10/2026.

The determination is NOT VERIFIED. The current revision cannot be relied on for the excavation. Item 048 remains Open and the 08/10/2026 start is not released. The design's groundwater and stratigraphic values are correct, but its engineered-fill unit weight and undrained shear strength are not supported by the record; the toe-embedment, anchor-bond, sheet-pile flexure and wall-deflection checks fail on the record-based inputs, and the anchor bond also fails the 2.0 criterion on the designer's own sealed inputs (108.6 / 56.2 = 1.93); the base-heave check passes only at the controlled head and fails at the design's own 727.0 ft stop-work trigger or with 0.5 ft of overdig; and the separately sealed Block B dewatering plan, the mat cut and temporary edge support, and the interface with the completed Block B mat, piles and K-5 joint are missing. Section 5 sets out what must be produced, by whom, and what this means for 08/10/2026.


2.  DOCUMENTS REVIEWED

The review was made against the following record. Revisions and dates are as stated in the documents. Where a document has been superseded in whole or in part, the governing part is identified.

Documents reviewed but not relied on: Rev.1 Section 2 and Section 3.4 dry-excavation assumption (Section 3.4 is superseded by Rev.2 R2.1; Section 2 remains in force but is contradicted by R2.1); 31-DW-A Block A well-point details (outside Block B); Calculation CB-GEO-004 (pile design, Item 049) and CB-STR-011 (mat design, Item 050), used only for interface checks; Sheet S-310/CB-STR-018 (podium, Item 055). The Rev.2 supplement is not entered in the Submittal Register; 31-SH-B Rev.1 is recorded as "Under review" as of 07/13/2026. The Block B field-density reports FDR-BB-01 through FDR-BB-14, referred to in the fill records, were requested but are not in the review file; that absence is a condition in Section 5, and 133.2 pcf is treated as a specified/derived value, not a measured one. All documents cited in Table 2-1 are the current revisions in the project record: GIR Rev.2 supersedes GIR Rev.1; DBM Rev.2 supersedes DBM Rev.1; Spec 31 20 00 Rev.3 supersedes Rev.2; S-101/S-201 Rev.4 supersede prior issues; A-501 Rev.3 supersedes prior revisions. Rev.1 of 31-SH-B is used only for the sections Rev.2 leaves in force, as identified in Finding 1.


3.  BASIS OF REVIEW

Precedence. DBM §1 states that the DBM governs all Package A calculations and controls subordinate documents; DBM §9 states that the GIR remains controlling for all soil parameters and any conflict is resolved in favour of the GIR. The GIR Rev.2 is therefore the governing source for groundwater, stratigraphy and soil strength. Rev.2's supersession matrix is applied only to the sections it expressly supersedes; sections left in force are checked for consistency with the new loads and geometry. RFI 104 and A-501 Rev.3 govern the permitted wall-to-mat joints; Spec 31 20 00 Articles 3.4.B and 3.6 govern fill acceptance and settlement; 31-DW-A Articles 1.2 and 4.2 govern the scope of dewatering. The primary verification case uses the least conservative record values — the GIR upper-bound su of 1,100 psf and the specified fill at optimum moisture (133.2 pcf) — so that a failure cannot be attributed to an adverse choice of input. The stricter bound permitted by the record — su 900 psf and fill at the +2% moisture limit (135.6 pcf) — is run in Tables 4-2 to 4-4; both cases fail, so the determination does not depend on which reading is applied. The controlled head of 726.5 ft is used for the base-heave check, and the 727.0 ft trigger and the 0.5 ft overdig case are also checked.

Table 3-1 — Governing parameters applied

Table 3-2 — Acceptance criteria applied

Method. The reviewer independently recomputed the active pressure (layered effective stress with hydrostatic water), passive resistance (total stress, su), free-earth toe moment, anchor force and bond, sheet-pile bending, wall deflection, base heave and dewatering consolidation. The designer's arithmetic was reproduced where the inputs are the same; differences are identified. The 133.2 pcf fill unit weight is a value derived from the specified acceptance criteria, not a measured Block B result: 95% of the Proctor maximum dry density 128.4 pcf at the 9.2% optimum moisture gives γtotal = 0.95 × 128.4 × 1.092 = 133.2 pcf (132.0 to 135.6 pcf over the permitted moisture window). The Block B field-density reports FDR-BB-01 through FDR-BB-14 referred to by the fill records are not in the review file; the only field-density report on file, SF-26-0708 (07/09/2026), is Block A fill tested against a different D698 Proctor (118.6 pcf, Wexford Ridge Phase 1 borrow). The 133.2 pcf value is therefore the specified minimum-at-optimum, and production of the FDR-BB reports is a required verification item (Section 5). The GIR su range of 900 to 1,100 psf is used; 1,100 psf is the upper bound and therefore the least conservative record value. The design's 1,400 psf is not supported by the GIR or the index data.


4.  FINDINGS

Finding 1 — Current revision and document status

Rev.2 is sealed and signed by B. A. Halvard, PE (Ohio P.E. No. E-58730, expires 12/31/2027) on 07/13/2026, so it is a valid later revision to the extent it supersedes Rev.1. However, the supersession matrix leaves Rev.1 Sections 1, 2, 3.1–3.3, 4.1, 4.2, 8, 11.3, 11.4, 12 and 13 in force. Four of those are inconsistent with Rev.2: (a) Section 2 still records the dry-excavation assumption of 31-DW-A, which Rev.2 Section 1 withdraws; (b) Section 11.3 still specifies a 28-ft PZ-35 single mill length, while Rev.2 R2.4 uses 30.5-ft sheets to tip El. 719.5; (c) Section 8's overturning and sliding checks use the Rev.1 loads (17,844 lb/ft) and toe El. 722.0, not the Rev.2 loads (19,610 lb/ft) and toe El. 719.5; (d) Section 13.1 item 2 still starts the Block A dewatering system (31-DW-A) 14 days before excavation, whereas Rev.2 relies on the Block B relief wells. In addition, the Rev.2 supplement is not logged in the Submittal Register (31-SH-B Rev.1 remains "Under review" as of 07/13/2026), and the Rev.1 Section 13 shoring drawings are not in the review file. The package is therefore not a complete, internally consistent design even before the numerical checks.

Finding 2 — Groundwater and stratigraphy are correctly stated

The GIR, the 19-round boring-log/monitoring record through 06/28/2026 and the Field Observation Report support the design water table El. 742.0 (range El. 741.6–742.4), the confined head El. 738.0 (range El. 737.7–738.3), the top of the confined aquifer El. 720.0, and the clay aquitard El. 738.0–720.0 (18 ft, 120 pcf). The shallow readings are from standpipes P-01 (B-01), P-03 (B-03) and P-09 (B-09), all outside the Block B plant-room footprint; the deep head is read at P-04 (B-04, inside the footprint) and P-08 (B-08). B-04 and B-06, inside the footprint, confirm the clay top and base, not the shallow water table in the fill. There is no shallow piezometer inside the Block B footprint; the fill record (Note 5) reports no free water during placement, including lifts crossing El. 742.0, so the El. 742.0 design value is conservative and appropriate, supported by the surrounding record rather than by a Block B shallow reading. The groundwater values in Rev.2 are therefore verified and can be carried forward. What is not verified is the design's response: Rev.2 introduces active depressurization to El. 726.5 (11.5 ft of drawdown), whereas 31-DW-A Rev.1 and register Item 006 record a Block B cutoff wall toed at El. 722.0 with no active drawdown. That is a change of strategy, not a groundwater reading.

Finding 3 — The engineered-fill unit weight is understated (118 pcf vs 133.2 pcf)

Rev.2 uses 118 pcf for the 12 ft of engineered fill from El. 750.0 to El. 738.0 (R2.3). That is the GIR design unit weight for the upper sand, not for the compacted structural fill. The fill placement record RB-FPR-BB-2025 records 14 lifts over 12 ft from 10/06/2025 to 11/02/2025, accepted to 95% of the D1557 maximum 128.4 pcf at 9.2% optimum moisture; the corresponding total unit weight is 0.95 × 128.4 × 1.092 = 133.2 pcf (132.0–135.6 pcf over the permitted moisture window). Using 118 pcf understates the retained fill weight by about 11%. The 133.2 pcf is derived from the specified acceptance criteria, not measured: the Block B field-density reports FDR-BB-01 through FDR-BB-14 referred to by the fill records are not in the review file, and the only field-density report on file (SF-26-0708, 07/09/2026) is Block A fill against a different D698 Proctor (118.6 pcf). Until the FDR-BB reports or a Kelbrook/Vantree confirmation of the placed fill are produced, 133.2 pcf is a specified/derived value, and the design is also checked at the design's 118 pcf. The determination does not depend on the fill value: at 118 pcf with su 1,100 psf the toe FS is 0.84 and the flexure FS is 0.88, both below 1.50.

Table 4-1 — Active lateral load, Rev.2 inputs vs specified fill

The reviewer's layered integration reproduces the R2.3 load of 19,610 lb/ft but gives a driving moment of 227,532 ft-lb/ft, 4.1% below the 237,293 ft-lb/ft stated in R2.3. The difference is in R2.3's soil moment: the stated pressure distribution (Psoil 11,622.8 lb/ft, resultant at 9.84 ft below the anchor) integrates to 114,380 ft-lb/ft, not the 124,141 ft-lb/ft in Table 2 of R2.3; the stated total is therefore conservative by 4.1%. R2.4's 1.55 becomes 1.62 on the actual integral of its own pressures; even 1.55 is only 3.3% above the 1.50 criterion, so the design's toe margin is thin. The specified fill increases the total horizontal load by 6.1% and reduces pn by 7.3% even at su 1,400 psf; the driver is the 5.9% increase in σv. The significant effect of the fill unit weight is on the passive resistance: even retaining the designer's su of 1,400 psf, the toe factor of safety falls from 1.62 (reviewer's reproduction) or 1.55 (Rev.2) to 1.43, below the required 1.50. The fill unit weight alone therefore fails the toe check; it also understates the anchor demand, flexure and deflection.

Finding 4 — The undrained shear strength is not supported by the GIR (1,400 psf vs 900–1,100 psf)

Rev.1 §3.2 and Rev.2 R2.4 use su = 1,400 psf. GIR §6.3 reports su = 900–1,100 psf from field vane and unconsolidated-undrained triaxial testing; the index and consolidation data contain no 1,400 psf value. DBM §9 makes the GIR controlling for soil parameters. A 1,400 psf value would require site-specific testing and a sealed geotechnical confirmation, neither of which is in the record. The reviewer notes that Calculation CB-GEO-004 uses an average su of 1,820 psf for pile shaft adhesion; that value is also outside the GIR range and is a separate inconsistency to be resolved under Item 049, but it cannot support the shoring value. Applying the upper bound of the logged range (1,100 psf) is the least conservative record-based value.

With specified fill and su 1,100 psf: pn = 4(1,100) − 3,288 = 1,112 psf (vs 2,494 psf design); Pp = 1,112 × 6.5 = 7,225 lb/ft (vs 16,211); MR = 7,225 × 22.75 = 164,374 ft-lb/ft (vs 368,800); toe FS = 164,374 / 239,786 = 0.69. At su 900 psf, FS = 0.19. The required embedment at these inputs is about 12.6 ft (tip about El. 713.4) if clay passive is used over the full depth; the design provides 6.5 ft. At the stricter bound (fill 135.6 pcf, su 900 psf), pn = 283 psf and FS = 0.17. The 1,400 psf value is the single largest non-conservative input in the design.

Finding 5 — Toe embedment fails on record-based inputs

Table 4-2 — Toe embedment factor of safety (criterion FS ≥ 1.50; D = 6.5 ft, tip El. 719.5)

Only the designer's 118 pcf / 1,400 psf case passes. Neither input is supported by the record. The toe check cannot be carried forward. A revised design must either increase the embedment (about 12.6 ft at the specified-fill / 1,100 psf inputs, tip about El. 713.4, which penetrates the aquifer), add a second anchor level, or otherwise reduce the load. The current tip El. 719.5 is 0.5 ft into the aquifer; the design states that the sheet is not a cutoff and relies on the relief wells, but GIR §9.6 requires every penetration of the clay to be sealed at the aquitard. No interlock seal detail is in the record, and no seepage or piping check at the toe or along the sheet-soil interface is included. The 30.5-ft sheet also conflicts with Rev.1 §11.3's 28-ft sheet (Finding 1).

Finding 6 — The anchor bond zone is in clay, not dense sand and gravel; bond and proof test fail

The anchor is at El. 745.5, inclined 20° below horizontal, with 25 ft free length and 24 ft bond length (49 ft total). At 20° the anchor tip is at El. 745.5 − 49 sin 20° = El. 728.74. The bond zone runs from El. 736.95 to El. 728.74, entirely within the CL clay (El. 738.0–720.0). It does not reach the dense sand and gravel below El. 720.0; to do so would require (745.5 − 720.0)/sin 20° = 74.6 ft total. The 20 psi bond stress used in R2.5 is the FHWA-IF-99-015 Table 4 value for dense sand and gravel; it is not applicable to the clay actually penetrated. At the stiff-clay end of the same table (10 psi), the 24-ft bond gives Q = π × 0.5 × 24 × 10 × 144 = 54.3 kips, below the Rev.2 design load of 56.2 kips and far below the specified-fill design load of 102.0 kips. On the designer's own sealed inputs the bond factor of safety is 108.6 / 56.2 = 1.93, below the 2.0 factor the design criteria apply (FHWA-IF-99-015 Table 4 / PTI DC35.1; Table 3-2); R2.5's statement that 1.93 is "adequate" is therefore not correct on its own numbers.

Table 4-3 — Anchor demand, bond capacity and proof test (6 ft spacing, 20°; 24-ft bond, 6-in diameter)

Even if the bond were in sand, the specified-fill / 1,100 psf demand gives FS 1.06 at 20 psi, below the 2.0 the design criteria apply; the proof test of 135.7 kips exceeds the 108.6-kip bond capacity, so the anchor cannot be proof-tested to 1.33 × design. On the designer's own inputs the bond FS is 1.93, still below 2.0. The 0.75 × design lock-off at the specified-fill demand is 76.5 kips, which exceeds the 54.3-kip 10 psi clay bond capacity (1.41 ×), so the anchor cannot be locked off without overloading the bond. On the mat sides, the 49-ft anchors extend about 46 ft horizontally from the wall at El. 745.5, beneath the existing mat and across the 48-pile group; no clash or clearance check is in the record. RFI 048 only addresses 6-in clear to wall reinforcement. The anchor design cannot be carried forward.

Finding 7 — Sheet-pile flexure fails on record-based inputs

With Rev.2 inputs, Mmax = 62.4 kip-ft/ft at El. 733.1, Mallow = 121 kip-ft/ft and FS = 1.94; the reviewer reproduces 62.45 kip-ft/ft. With specified fill and su 1,400 psf, Mmax rises to 83.8 kip-ft/ft (FS 1.45, below 1.5); with specified fill and su 1,100 psf, Mmax is 162.4 kip-ft/ft (FS 0.75) and exceeds the allowable moment. The flexure check fails on the record-based inputs and cannot be carried forward. Table 4-4 summarises this and the deflection check.

Table 4-4 — Flexure and deflection

Finding 8 — Wall deflection exceeds H/200

Rev.2 predicts 1.3 in at El. 738.0 against H/200 = 1.44 in, a margin of only 0.14 in. Scaling the designer's own method by the increase in maximum moment gives about 1.74 in for specified fill and su 1,400 psf, and about 3.4 in for specified fill and su 1,100 psf, both above 1.44 in. The method is not independently reproducible from the record (no soil modulus or stiffness is stated), so the check is not verified; a revised deflection analysis is required. The deflection check cannot be carried forward.

Finding 9 — Base heave passes only at the controlled point; the operating envelope fails

The arithmetic is correct: W = 6.0 × 120 = 720 psf; 0.9W = 648 psf; at the controlled head El. 726.5, u = (726.5 − 720.0) × 62.4 = 405.6 psf; FS = 648 / 405.6 = 1.60, above 1.50. But the operating envelope is not. At the R2.7 stop-work trigger El. 727.0, u = 436.8 psf and FS = 1.48, below 1.50. If the plug is 5.5 ft (0.5 ft of overdig), FS at 726.5 is 1.46 and at 727.0 is 1.36. At the initial head El. 738.0, FS is 0.58. The design has only a 6.7% margin at the controlled point, and its own trigger permits non-compliance. Pumping is the sole safeguard; there is no standby pump or power, automatic alarm, or response plan in the record.

Table 4-5 — Base-heave factor of safety vs head and plug thickness (criterion FS ≥ 1.50)

The base-heave formula can be carried forward only with the following conditions: stop-work trigger at or below El. 726.5 (preferably 726.0), no excavation below El. 726.0, continuous pumping with standby pumps and standby power, automatic high-head alarm, and a permanent plant-room slab designed for the full confined head El. 738.0. As written, the check is not verified.

Finding 10 — Global stability and overturning are stale and not updated for Rev.2

Rev.1 §8 remains in force under the Rev.2 matrix but was not updated. Its FS 2.06 uses the Rev.1 loads (17,844 lb/ft), passive 2,490 lb/ft and toe El. 722.0; none of these apply to Rev.2 (19,610 lb/ft, allowable passive 10,807 lb/ft, toe El. 719.5). Recomputing the §8.2 check on the Rev.2 geometry gives FS 0.94 for the designer's inputs, 1.04 for specified fill and su 1,400 psf, and 1.43 for specified fill and su 1,100 psf, not 2.06. That is an indicator that §8 was not updated, not a separate free-earth check; §8.2 treats the tieback reaction as an external resisting force, whereas R2.4 uses the free-earth formulation. The §8.1 "wall-free" sliding FS of 0.28 is not a design check with the tieback. The global stability section must be reissued. The design also does not check lateral support to the existing mat and piles, excavation unloading and heave, or vibration; those are addressed in Findings 11 and 12.

Finding 11 — The Block B dewatering plan is missing, and the excavation affects permanent work already built

31-DW-A Rev.1 Article 1.2 expressly limits the plan to Block A and says the Block B plant-room will be addressed by a separate delegated design; Article 4.2 says the plan shall not be relied on for any design that assumes a reduction in the confined head below El. 738.0. Rev.2 introduces exactly such a reduction (to El. 726.5) but is a shoring supplement, not the separately sealed dewatering and hydrogeologic analysis 31-DW-A requires. It gives four 8-in relief wells and a target head, and it does specify continuous piezometer readings during the mandatory 72-hour confirmation hold (R2.1) and a stop-work trigger at El. 727.0 (R2.7). Rev.2 uses 118 pcf for the 12 ft of engineered fill from El. 750.0 to El. 738.0 (R2.3). That is the GIR design unit weight for the upper sand, not for the compacted structural fill. The fill placement record RB-FPR-BB-2025 records 14 lifts over 12 ft from 10/06/2025 to 11/02/2025, accepted to 95% of the D1557 maximum 128.4 pcf at 9.2% optimum moisture; the corresponding total unit weight is 0.95 × 128.4 × 1.092 = 133.2 pcf (132.0–135.6 pcf over the permitted moisture window). Using 118 pcf understates the retained fill weight by about 11%. The 133.2 pcf is derived from the specified acceptance criteria, not measured: the Block B field-density reports FDR-BB-01 through FDR-BB-14 referred to by the fill records are not in the review file, and the only field-density report on file (SF-26-0708, 07/09/2026) is Block A fill against a different D698 Proctor (118.6 pcf). Until the FDR-BB reports or a Kelbrook/Vantree confirmation of the placed fill are produced, 133.2 pcf is a specified/derived value, and the design is also checked at the design's 118 pcf. The determination does not depend on the fill value: at 118 pcf with su 1,100 psf the toe FS is 0.84 and the flexure FS is 0.88, both below 1.50. 

The reviewer's layered integration reproduces the R2.3 load of 19,610 lb/ft and gives a driving moment of 237,275 ft-lb/ft, within 0.01% of the 237,293 ft-lb/ft stated in R2.3; the design's moment is correct. R2.4's 1.55 is only 3.3% above the 1.50 criterion, so the design's toe margin is thin. The specified fill increases the total horizontal load by 6.1% and the driving moment by 5.3% (237,275 to 249,975 ft-lb/ft), and reduces pn by 7.3% even at su 1,400 psf; the driver is the 5.9% increase in σv. The significant effect of the fill unit weight is on the passive resistance: even retaining the designer's su of 1,400 psf, the toe factor of safety falls from 1.55 to 1.37, below the required 1.50. The fill unit weight alone therefore fails the toe check; it also understates the anchor demand, flexure and deflection. 

With specified fill and su 1,100 psf: pn = 4(1,100) − 3,288 = 1,112 psf (vs 2,494 psf design); Pp = 1,112 × 6.5 = 7,225 lb/ft (vs 16,211); MR = 7,225 × 22.75 = 164,374 ft-lb/ft (vs 368,800); toe FS = 164,374 / 249,975 = 0.66. At su 900 psf, FS = 0.18. The required embedment at these inputs is about 13.0 ft (tip about El. 713.0) if clay passive is used over the full depth; the design provides 6.5 ft. At the stricter bound (fill 135.6 pcf, su 900 psf), pn = 283 psf and FS = 0.17. The 1,400 psf value is the single largest non-conservative input in the design. 

Only the designer's 118 pcf / 1,400 psf case passes, and only by 3.3%. Neither input is supported by the record. The toe check cannot be carried forward. A revised design must either increase the embedment (about 13.0 ft at the specified-fill / 1,100 psf inputs, tip about El. 713.0, which penetrates the aquifer), add a second anchor level, or otherwise reduce the load. The current tip El. 719.5 is 0.5 ft into the aquifer; the design states that the sheet is not a cutoff and relies on the relief wells, but GIR §9.6 requires every penetration of the clay to be sealed at the aquitard. No interlock seal detail is in the record, and no seepage or piping check at the toe or along the sheet-soil interface is included. The 30.5-ft sheet also conflicts with Rev.1 §11.3's 28-ft sheet (Finding 1). 

With Rev.2 inputs, Mmax = 62.4 kip-ft/ft at El. 733.1, Mallow = 121 kip-ft/ft and FS = 1.94; the reviewer reproduces 62.45 kip-ft/ft. With specified fill and su 1,400 psf, Mmax rises to 83.8 kip-ft/ft (FS 1.45, below 1.5); with specified fill and su 1,100 psf, Mmax is 162.4 kip-ft/ft (FS 0.75) and exceeds the allowable moment. The flexure check fails on the record-based inputs and cannot be carried forward. Table 4-4 summarises this and the deflection check. 

Rev.1 §8 remains in force under the Rev.2 matrix but was not updated. Its FS 2.06 uses the Rev.1 loads (17,844 lb/ft), passive 2,490 lb/ft and toe El. 722.0; none of these apply to Rev.2 (19,610 lb/ft, allowable passive 10,807 lb/ft, toe El. 719.5). Recomputing the §8.2 check on the Rev.2 geometry gives FS 0.97 for the designer's inputs, 1.08 for specified fill and su 1,400 psf, and 1.48 for specified fill and su 1,100 psf, not 2.06. That is an indicator that §8 was not updated, not a separate free-earth check; §8.2 treats the tieback reaction as an external resisting force, whereas R2.4 uses the free-earth formulation. The §8.1 "wall-free" sliding FS of 0.28 is not a design check with the tieback. The global stability section must be reissued. The design also does not check lateral support to the existing mat and piles, excavation unloading and heave, or vibration; those are addressed in Findings 11 and 12.

8.1 Sliding
The wall does not translate horizontally as a rigid body because it is restrained by the tieback anchor at El. 745.5
(see Section 10) and by the passive block below subgrade. The tieback horizontal reaction (15.4 kips/ft, per
Section 7.3) is the direct restraint against horizontal translation of the upper wall; the passive block restrains
translation of the toe. Sliding is therefore not a rigid-body failure mode for this wall configuration; the applicable
checks are the anchor pull-out (Section 10) and the toe embedment (Section 9).
For completeness, and treating the sheet-pile section conservatively as a floating rigid strip with only the passive
